model.courtconnect.bridge_place_sport.name: bridge_place_sport
model.courtconnect.bridge_place_sport.description: Sports a place offers, with 'strong' or 'weak' evidence.
model.courtconnect.bridge_place_sport.raw_code:
-- Which sports a place offers, and how good the evidence is.
--   category          : Overture itself classifies it as a racket sport venue            -> strong
--   name_keyword      : a sport word appears in the business name
--        distinctive term ("padel", "squash", "table tennis" ...)                           -> strong
--        ambiguous term  ("real tennis" also matches "Camino Real Tennis Center")           -> weak (never counted as a venue)
with category_matches as (
    select p.place_id, s.sport_id, 'category' as match_type, p.category as matched_term, 'strong' as evidence
    from {{ ref('stg_overture_places') }} p
    join {{ ref('overture_category_map') }} m on m.overture_category = p.category
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_name = m.sport
),

name_matches as (
    select p.place_id, s.sport_id, 'name_keyword' as match_type, t.term as matched_term,
           case when t.reliability = 'distinctive' then 'strong' else 'weak' end as evidence
    from {{ ref('stg_overture_places') }} p
    join {{ ref('sport_search_terms') }} t on p.name_norm like '% ' || t.term || ' %'
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_name = t.sport
),

-- "Table Tennis Association" must not also count as plain "Tennis": drop a name match when a longer
-- matched term for the same place contains it.
name_matches_specific as (
    select a.*
    from name_matches a
    where not exists (
        select 1 from name_matches b
        where b.place_id = a.place_id
          and length(b.matched_term) > length(a.matched_term)
          and b.matched_term like '%' || a.matched_term || '%'
    )
),

-- Overture's category is dropped when the place's own name clearly says another sport: the name has a distinctive term for a
-- different sport ("table tennis" on a tennis_court) and, once that term is removed, no standalone word of the category sport is
-- left ("Anaheim Tennis and Pickleball Center" keeps Tennis; "Ararat Table Tennis" loses it). Ambiguous terms ("beach tennis") never
-- trigger this (Newport Beach Tennis Club is a real tennis club): use place_sport_overrides.csv for those.
-- "tennis", "racquet club" and "racket club" are generic (multi-sport tennis centres are common, and a pickleball_court inside a
-- "Tennis Center" is real), so they never contradict a category.
category_name_conflicts as (
    select distinct c.place_id, c.sport_id
    from category_matches c
    join {{ ref('stg_overture_places') }} p on p.place_id = c.place_id
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} cs on cs.sport_id = c.sport_id
    join name_matches_specific n on n.place_id = c.place_id
         and n.evidence = 'strong' and n.sport_id <> c.sport_id
         and n.matched_term not in ('tennis', 'racquet club', 'racket club')
    where not exists (
        select 1
        from {{ ref('sport_search_terms') }} own
        where trim(own.sport) = cs.sport_name
          and replace(p.name_norm, ' ' || n.matched_term || ' ', ' ') like '% ' || own.term || ' %'
    )
),

category_kept as (
    select c.*
    from category_matches c
    left join category_name_conflicts x on x.place_id = c.place_id and x.sport_id = c.sport_id
    where x.place_id is null
),

unioned as (
    select * from category_kept
    union all
    select * from name_matches_specific
),

ranked as (
    select *,
           row_number() over (
               partition by place_id, sport_id
               order by case evidence when 'strong' then 1 else 2 end, case match_type when 'category' then 1 else 2 end, matched_term
           ) as rn
    from unioned
),

base as (
    select place_id, sport_id, match_type, matched_term, evidence
    from ranked
    where rn = 1
),

-- Human review (seeds/place_sport_overrides.csv): verdict 'confirm' makes the match strong, 'reject' removes it.
overrides as (
    select o.place_id, s.sport_id, lower(trim(o.verdict)) as verdict
    from {{ ref('place_sport_overrides') }} o
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_name = trim(o.sport)
),

kept as (
    select b.*
    from base b
    left join overrides o on o.place_id = b.place_id and o.sport_id = b.sport_id
    where o.place_id is null
),

confirmed as (
    select place_id, sport_id, 'manual' as match_type, 'confirmed in review' as matched_term, 'strong' as evidence
    from overrides
    where verdict = 'confirm'
),

settled as (
    select * from kept
    union all
    select * from confirmed
),

-- A place that offers sport A also offers sport B where sport_also_played.csv says so (racquetball courts host 4-wall paddle).
-- The derived row keeps the evidence strength of the row it comes from, and its matched_term says why it is there.
also_played as (
    select s.place_id, d.sport_id, 'also_played' as match_type,
           'also played on ' || lower(trim(a.sport)) || ' courts' as matched_term, s.evidence
    from settled s
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} f on f.sport_id = s.sport_id
    join {{ ref('sport_also_played') }} a on trim(a.sport) = f.sport_name
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} d on d.sport_name = trim(a.also_sport)
    join {{ ref('stg_overture_places') }} p on p.place_id = s.place_id
    where not exists (select 1 from settled x where x.place_id = s.place_id and x.sport_id = d.sport_id)
      -- only_surfaces set: Overture places carry no court surface, so the sport is not passed on
      and nullif(trim(a.only_surfaces), '') is null
      -- only_access set (Micro Pickleball: public): Overture has no access data, so the sport is not passed on
      and nullif(trim(a.only_access), '') is null
      -- exclude_name_inferred = yes: the place's sport came from its name (name_keyword), not from an Overture category or a human
      -- confirmation, so the sport is not passed on; only known (tagged or confirmed) courts count
      and not (lower(trim(coalesce(a.exclude_name_inferred, ''))) = 'yes' and s.match_type = 'name_keyword')
      -- exclude_private_members = yes: Overture has no access tag, so a club-style name (country / athletic / racquet / tennis / golf /
      -- swim club, "private", "members") counts as private or members-only and does not pass the sport on
      and not (lower(trim(coalesce(a.exclude_private_members, ''))) = 'yes'
               and (p.name_norm like '% country club %' or p.name_norm like '% athletic club %' or p.name_norm like '% racquet club %'
                    or p.name_norm like '% tennis club %' or p.name_norm like '% golf club %' or p.name_norm like '% swim club %'
                    or p.name_norm like '% private %' or p.name_norm like '% members %'))
)

select * from settled
union all
select * from also_played

model.courtconnect.dim_court.name: dim_court
model.courtconnect.dim_court.description: One row per physical court / sports-centre record from OpenStreetMap.
model.courtconnect.dim_court.raw_code:
select
    c.court_id,
    k.cluster_label                                           as venue_key,
    md5(k.cluster_label)                                      as venue_id,
    c.record_kind,
    c.court_name,
    c.lat,
    c.lon,
    c.surface_type,
    c.setting,
    c.is_lit,
    c.access_type,
    c.is_free,
    c.operator_name,
    try_cast(c.courts_count_raw as integer)                   as courts_count,
    c.osm_leisure_type,
    c.website,
    c.phone,
    c.opening_hours,
    c.address_line,
    c.city,
    p.parent_name,
    p.parent_kind,
    p.parent_area,
    c.extracted_at,
    c.region
from {{ ref('stg_osm_courts') }} c
join {{ ref('int_court_clusters') }} k on k.court_id = c.court_id
left join {{ ref('int_court_parent') }} p on p.court_id = c.court_id

model.courtconnect.dim_place.name: dim_place
model.courtconnect.dim_place.description: One row per Overture place, linked to an OSM venue when one is within place_match_radius_m metres.
model.courtconnect.dim_place.raw_code:
-- One row per Overture place, linked to an OSM venue when one is within `place_match_radius_m` metres.
-- venue_id is the venue the place belongs to: the matched OSM venue, otherwise a venue of its own.
with strong as (
    select place_id, count(distinct sport_id) as strong_sport_count
    from {{ ref('bridge_place_sport') }}
    where evidence = 'strong'
    group by 1
),

-- Same street address (suite/unit stripped) in the same city = one facility: places Overture lists twice, or an academy
-- sharing a club's building, get one venue_id (the smallest place_id of the group) so the map shows one pin.
-- Only strong-sport places that no OSM venue claimed take part; places without a street number are never grouped;
-- places listed in seeds/place_no_group.csv (different organisations at one address) are never grouped.
addr as (
    select
        p.place_id,
        trim(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(replace(replace(lower(p.address_line), ',', ' '), '  ', ' '), ' (ste|suite|unit|apt|cabana|bldg|building)[ .#].*$', ''), ' #.*$', '')) as street_key,
        lower(trim(p.city)) as city_key
    from {{ ref('stg_overture_places') }} p
    left join {{ ref('int_place_venue_match') }} m on m.place_id = p.place_id
    join strong s on s.place_id = p.place_id
    where m.place_id is null and p.address_line is not null
      and p.place_id not in (select place_id from {{ ref('place_no_group') }})  -- separate businesses at one address stay separate pins
),

place_group as (
    select place_id,
           min(place_id) over (partition by street_key, city_key) as group_place_id
    from addr
    where street_key between '0' and '9z' and city_key is not null
)

select
    p.place_id,
    p.place_name,
    p.category,
    p.lat,
    p.lon,
    p.confidence,
    p.website,
    {{ website_domain('p.website') }}                         as website_domain,
    {{ website_status('p.website', 'w.status') }}             as website_status,
    p.phone,
    p.address_line,
    p.city,
    p.postcode,
    p.license,
    p.release,
    p.region,
    m.venue_id                                                as matched_venue_id,
    m.distance_m                                              as match_distance_m,
    coalesce(m.venue_id, md5('place/' || coalesce(g.group_place_id, p.place_id))) as venue_id,
    coalesce(s.strong_sport_count, 0)                         as strong_sport_count,
    coalesce(s.strong_sport_count, 0) > 0                     as has_strong_sport
from {{ ref('stg_overture_places') }} p
left join {{ ref('int_place_venue_match') }} m on m.place_id = p.place_id
left join strong s on s.place_id = p.place_id
left join place_group g on g.place_id = p.place_id
left join {{ ref('stg_website_checks') }} w on w.domain = {{ website_domain('p.website') }}

model.courtconnect.dim_sport.name: dim_sport
model.courtconnect.dim_sport.description: One row per racket sport. The reference dimension for the whole platform.

competitive_tier.name: competitive_tier
competitive_tier.description: INFERRED from the sheet's popularity_class, competing and org columns (established / organized / casual); never a claim about any venue.

model.courtconnect.dim_sport.raw_code:
select
    sport_id,
    sport_name,
    sport_family,
    popularity_class,
    governing_body,
    players_min,
    players_max,
    court_length_ft,
    court_width_ft,
    net_type,
    net_height_in,
    net_height_alt_in,
    surface_lc like '%concrete%'                              as plays_on_concrete,
    surface_lc like '%sand%'                                  as plays_on_sand,
    surface_lc like '%grass%'                                 as plays_on_grass,
    surface_lc like '%indoor%'                                as plays_indoors,
    -- the one surface a sport needs when the sheet lists no concrete, grass or sand for it (Padel = turf, Teq = curved table); null = no special surface.
    -- "Indoor/Outdoor" is not indoor-only. The "Find by court" dialog only offers such a sport courts of the same kind.
    case
        when surface_lc like '%concrete%' or surface_lc like '%grass%' or surface_lc like '%sand%' then null
        when surface_lc like '%curved table%' then 'curved_table'
        when surface_lc like '%tabletop%'     then 'tabletop'
        when surface_lc like '%turf%'         then 'turf'
        when surface_lc like '%aluminum%'     then 'aluminum'
        when surface_lc like '%indoor%' and surface_lc not like '%outdoor%' then 'indoor'
    end                                                       as special_surface,
    base_gear,
    gear_on_amazon_or_online,
    competitive_status,
    -- INFERRED tier from the sheet only (no venue or event data): 'established' = a world-federation sport (class World Official, competing),
    -- 'organized' = competing with a named governing body that is not flagged defunct/unsure, 'casual' = everything else.
    case
        when competitive_status = 'Competitive' and popularity_class = 'World Official' then 'established'
        when competitive_status = 'Competitive' and governing_body is not null
             and governing_body not like '%?%' and lower(governing_body) not like '%defunct%' then 'organized'
        else 'casual'
    end                                                       as competitive_tier,
    year_origin,
    official_url
from {{ ref('stg_sports') }}

model.courtconnect.dim_wall.name: dim_wall
model.courtconnect.dim_wall.description: One row per hitting wall (hand-curated plus OSM-mapped), kept apart from venues.

access.name: access
access.description: Same vocabulary as venues (access_type); blank = not known (never read as public).

model.courtconnect.dim_wall.raw_code:
-- One row per hitting wall: hand-curated (seeds/manual_walls.csv) plus those mapped in OpenStreetMap. Blank flags stay NULL
-- (unknown); `confirmation` says how we know (reported / official by hand, tagged = from OSM tags only).
-- A hand-added one-wall / three-wall court (a report or official page says what it is) beats the OSM default for the same court:
-- OSM walls within `wall_group_radius_m` of one are dropped, so the confirmed pin is the only one shown. Backboards and
-- other types don't hide OSM walls (a backboard is a different structure from a handball court nearby).
select * from {{ ref('stg_manual_walls') }}
union all
select o.*
from {{ ref('stg_osm_walls') }} o
where not exists (
    select 1
    from {{ ref('stg_manual_walls') }} m
    where m.wall_type in ('one_wall', 'three_wall', 'one_wall;three_wall')
      and abs(m.lat - o.lat) < 0.01
      and sqrt(
              power((m.lat - o.lat) * 110540, 2)
            + power((m.lon - o.lon) * cos(radians(m.lat)) * 111320, 2)
          ) <= {{ var('wall_group_radius_m') }}
)

model.courtconnect.ref_sport_fit.name: ref_sport_fit
model.courtconnect.ref_sport_fit.description: Physical sport-fit reference (INFERRED, not a venue claim): guest sport's court rectangle fits inside the host sport's (rotation allowed, shared surface), from the sheet's court dimensions. Not yet exported to the map.
model.courtconnect.ref_sport_fit.raw_code:
-- Physical sport-fit reference: which sports' playing areas fit inside another sport's court footprint.
-- Derived only from the sheet's court dimensions (dim_sport), so it is INFERRED, never "confirmed":
-- "fits" means the guest court's rectangle fits inside the host's (rotation allowed) and they share a surface type.
-- It does not say a venue allows the sport or has lines/nets for it. Not wired into the map yet.
with s as (
    select
        sport_name,
        greatest(court_length_ft, court_width_ft) as long_ft,
        least(court_length_ft, court_width_ft)    as short_ft,
        plays_on_concrete, plays_on_grass, plays_on_sand
    from {{ ref('dim_sport') }}
    where court_length_ft is not null and court_width_ft is not null
)

select
    h.sport_name                                         as host_sport,
    g.sport_name                                         as guest_sport,
    g.long_ft * g.short_ft                               as guest_area_sqft,
    h.long_ft * h.short_ft                               as host_area_sqft,
    round((g.long_ft * g.short_ft) / (h.long_ft * h.short_ft), 3) as area_ratio,
    -- 2+ guest courts side by side (same orientation) fit inside the host
    (floor(h.long_ft / g.long_ft) * floor(h.short_ft / g.short_ft)) as guest_courts_that_fit,
    'inferred'                                           as confirmation
from s h
join s g
  on g.sport_name <> h.sport_name
 and g.long_ft  <= h.long_ft
 and g.short_ft <= h.short_ft
 and (   (h.plays_on_concrete and g.plays_on_concrete)
      or (h.plays_on_grass    and g.plays_on_grass)
      or (h.plays_on_sand     and g.plays_on_sand))

model.courtconnect.int_court_clusters.name: int_court_clusters
model.courtconnect.int_court_clusters.description: Groups courts into facilities: connected components of the court-pairs graph, found in plain SQL by 8 label-propagation passes (each court adopts the smallest label among its neighbours). assert_clusters_converged proves 8 passes were enough.
model.courtconnect.int_court_clusters.raw_code:
-- Groups courts into facilities: connected components of the "within N metres" graph.
-- Portable SQL (no recursion, no UDFs): every court starts with its own id as a label and,
-- on each pass, adopts the smallest label among its neighbours. Labels flood outward from
-- the smallest id in each group, so after enough passes everyone in a facility shares one label.
-- `changed_in_last_pass` lets a dbt test prove we ran enough passes (see assert_clusters_converged).
{% set passes = 8 %}

with pairs as (
    select * from {{ ref('int_court_pairs') }}
),

l0 as (
    select court_id, court_id as label from {{ ref('stg_osm_courts') }}
)
{% for i in range(1, passes + 1) %}
, l{{ i }} as (
    select
        c.court_id,
        least(c.label, coalesce(min(n.label), c.label)) as label
    from l{{ i - 1 }} c
    left join pairs p on p.court_a = c.court_id
    left join l{{ i - 1 }} n on n.court_id = p.court_b
    group by c.court_id, c.label
)
{% endfor %}

select
    a.court_id,
    a.label                       as cluster_label,
    (a.label <> b.label)          as changed_in_last_pass
from l{{ passes }} a
join l{{ passes - 1 }} b on b.court_id = a.court_id

model.courtconnect.int_court_pairs.name: int_court_pairs
model.courtconnect.int_court_pairs.description: Every pair of courts within venue_radius_m of each other, plus pairs inside the same named school, park or club within parent_merge_radius_m. Courts are bucketed into a grid so each is compared only with its own and the 8 neighbouring cells, which scales to a whole state.
model.courtconnect.int_court_pairs.raw_code:
-- Every pair of courts within `venue_radius_m` metres of each other (both directions), plus pairs of courts inside the
-- same named school/park/club/golf club that are within `parent_merge_radius_m` (a school's courts a few hundred
-- metres apart are one facility, not several). Matched on the lower-cased name, not the OSM id, because one school
-- or club is often mapped as several polygons.
-- Scales to a whole state: courts are bucketed into a grid whose cell is about one radius wide, and each court
-- is only compared with courts in its own and the 8 neighbouring cells (an equi-join, not a cross join).
{% set radius = var('venue_radius_m') %}
{% set cell = radius / 80000.0 %}

with cells as (
    select
        court_id, lat, lon,
        cast(floor(lat / {{ cell }}) as bigint) as cy,
        cast(floor(lon / {{ cell }}) as bigint) as cx
    from {{ ref('stg_osm_courts') }}
),

offsets as (
    select -1 as d union all select 0 union all select 1
),

-- The neighbour cell is computed in a CTE, not inside the join condition: with `b.cy = a.cy + dy.d` in the ON clause
-- DuckDB did not hash-join and the model took ~90 s for 27k courts; this form takes well under a second.
probe as (
    select a.court_id, a.lat, a.lon, a.cy + dy.d as ny, a.cx + dx.d as nx
    from cells a
    cross join offsets dy
    cross join offsets dx
)

select
    a.court_id as court_a,
    b.court_id as court_b
from probe a
join cells b
    on b.cy = a.ny
   and b.cx = a.nx
   and b.court_id <> a.court_id
where sqrt(
          power((a.lat - b.lat) * 110540, 2)
        + power((a.lon - b.lon) * cos(radians(a.lat)) * 111320, 2)
      ) <= {{ radius }}

union

select
    a.court_id as court_a,
    b.court_id as court_b
from {{ ref('int_court_parent') }} pa
join {{ ref('int_court_parent') }} pb
    on lower(pb.parent_name) = lower(pa.parent_name)
   and pb.court_id <> pa.court_id
join {{ ref('stg_osm_courts') }} a on a.court_id = pa.court_id
join {{ ref('stg_osm_courts') }} b on b.court_id = pb.court_id
where sqrt(
          power((a.lat - b.lat) * 110540, 2)
        + power((a.lon - b.lon) * cos(radians(a.lat)) * 111320, 2)
      ) <= {{ var('parent_merge_radius_m') }}
  -- a park whose courts belong to different facilities is listed in seeds/parent_merge_block.csv: only the 75 m rule links its courts (ADR 0030)
  and lower(pa.parent_name) not in (select lower(parent_name) from {{ ref('parent_merge_block') }})

union

-- hand-checked merges of court groups that are one facility (seeds/court_group_merge.csv), both directions
select court_id_a as court_a, court_id_b as court_b from {{ ref('court_group_merge') }}
union
select court_id_b as court_a, court_id_a as court_b from {{ ref('court_group_merge') }}

model.courtconnect.int_place_venue_match.name: int_place_venue_match
model.courtconnect.int_place_venue_match.description: Links each Overture place to the OSM venue it is part of, using four rules in order: distance, same_name, facility_name (named after the court's park, school or centre, or sharing its address) and inside_facility (pin inside a small park or school footprint, racquet-sport records only). `match_rule` records which rule fired. Every radius and rule was judged against the gold set (docs/gold_set_plan.md).
model.courtconnect.int_place_venue_match.raw_code:
-- Link each Overture place to the OSM venue it is part of. Three rules, strongest first (a place takes the first rule that fits):
--   distance       nearest OSM court/facility within `place_match_radius_m` metres
--   same_name      within `place_name_match_radius_m` when place and an OSM court carry the same name
--                  (Overture and OSM often put the same club's pin a little apart)
--   facility_name  within `place_facility_match_radius_m` when the place is named after the court's park/school/centre
--                  ("Memorial Park Tennis Courts" for courts mapped inside Memorial Park), or place and court/park share a street address.
--                  Added after the gold set found 17 of 19 checked unmatched places were such misses (docs/gold_set_plan.md).
--                  A bare city name inside a longer parent name ("Atascadero Pickleball Club" vs "Atascadero Unified School District") never counts (an equal name, "Tustin Sports Park", still does):
--                  radius 300 m (was 200) after the third gold slice, which showed this guard is needed there.
--   inside_facility  a place the three rules above leave unmatched joins a court's park/school/centre when its pin lies inside that
--                  feature's (small) bounding box, the nearest of that feature's courts is within `place_inside_match_radius_m`, the place is a
--                  racquet-sport lesson/court record (not a club, resort, league or gym: those are often a different business next door,
--                  e.g. Walnut Creek Racquet Club beside Heather Farm Park) and its name does not say another sport. Gold set, third slice.
--   seed_link      a hand-checked place -> court group link (place_venue_link.csv) for a place no radius reaches; beats every rule above.
-- Same grid-bucket trick as int_court_pairs, so it scales statewide.
{% set radius = var('place_match_radius_m') %}
{% set name_radius = var('place_name_match_radius_m') %}
{% set facility_radius = var('place_facility_match_radius_m') %}
{% set inside_radius = var('place_inside_match_radius_m') %}
{% set inside_max_area = var('place_inside_max_bbox_deg2') %}
{% set not_inside_words = ['club','resort','country','association','society','league','federation','table','ping','badminton','squash','racquetball','handball'] %}
{% set inside_categories = ['tennis_court','fitness_trainer','sports_and_recreation','sport_or_recreation_club','pickleball_court','park'] %}
{% set cell = name_radius / 80000.0 %}

with places as (
    select place_id, lower(trim(place_name)) as name_key, lower(place_name) as name_lc, category, {{ facility_key(normalize_name('place_name')) }} as fac_key,
           trim({{ normalize_name('city') }}) as city_key,
           case when address_line is not null and substr(trim(address_line), 1, 1) between '0' and '9'
                then {{ address_key('address_line') }} end as addr_key,
           lat, lon,
           cast(floor(lat / {{ cell }}) as bigint) as cy,
           cast(floor(lon / {{ cell }}) as bigint) as cx
    from {{ ref('stg_overture_places') }}
),

courts as (
    select c.court_id, lower(c.court_name) as name_key, c.lat, c.lon, md5(k.cluster_label) as venue_id, cp.parent_id, cp.parent_kind,
           -- golf courses / hotels have big irregular bounding boxes that swallow neighbours' courts (int_court_parent), so their names never count
           case when cp.parent_kind <> 'resort_or_other' then {{ facility_key(normalize_name('cp.parent_name')) }} end as parent_key,
           {{ address_key('c.address_line') }} as court_addr_key,
           {{ address_key('pr.address_line') }} as parent_addr_key,
           cast(floor(c.lat / {{ cell }}) as bigint) as cy,
           cast(floor(c.lon / {{ cell }}) as bigint) as cx
    from {{ ref('stg_osm_courts') }} c
    join {{ ref('int_court_clusters') }} k on k.court_id = c.court_id
    left join {{ ref('int_court_parent') }} cp on cp.court_id = c.court_id
    left join {{ ref('stg_osm_parents') }} pr on pr.parent_id = cp.parent_id
),

offsets as (
    select -1 as d union all select 0 union all select 1
),

candidates as (
    select
        p.place_id, c.venue_id, (p.name_key = c.name_key) as same_name,
        -- the distinctive part of the place name is, or contains, the park/school/centre name (or the reverse); 5+ characters so a stub never matches
        (length(trim(p.fac_key)) >= 5 and length(trim(c.parent_key)) >= 5 and not (trim(p.fac_key) = p.city_key and trim(c.parent_key) <> trim(p.fac_key))
         and (p.fac_key like '%' || c.parent_key || '%' or c.parent_key like '%' || p.fac_key || '%')) as facility_name,
        (p.addr_key is not null and length(p.addr_key) > 8
         and (p.addr_key = c.court_addr_key or p.addr_key = c.parent_addr_key)) as same_address,
        sqrt(power((p.lat - c.lat) * 110540, 2)
           + power((p.lon - c.lon) * cos(radians(p.lat)) * 111320, 2)) as distance_m
    from places p
    cross join offsets dy
    cross join offsets dx
    join courts c on c.cy = p.cy + dy.d and c.cx = p.cx + dx.d
),

ruled as (
    select place_id, venue_id, distance_m,
           case when distance_m <= {{ radius }} then 'distance'
                when same_name and distance_m <= {{ name_radius }} then 'same_name'
                when (facility_name or same_address) and distance_m <= {{ facility_radius }} then 'facility_name'
           end as match_rule
    from candidates
),

in_footprint as (
    select p.place_id, c.venue_id,
           sqrt(power((p.lat - c.lat) * 110540, 2) + power((p.lon - c.lon) * cos(radians(p.lat)) * 111320, 2)) as distance_m
    from places p
    join {{ ref('stg_osm_parents') }} par
      on p.lat between par.minlat and par.maxlat and p.lon between par.minlon and par.maxlon
    join courts c on c.parent_id = par.parent_id
    where par.kind_group in ('school', 'park', 'community', 'sports_facility')
      and par.bbox_area_deg2 <= {{ inside_max_area }}
      -- a human 'reject' in place_sport_overrides means the page names no courts or facility (ADR 0016): never place it by footprint
      and not exists (select 1 from {{ ref('place_sport_overrides') }} o where o.place_id = p.place_id and lower(trim(o.verdict)) = 'reject')
      and p.category in ({% for c in inside_categories %}'{{ c }}'{{ ',' if not loop.last }}{% endfor %})
      {% for w in not_inside_words %}and p.name_lc not like '%{{ w }}%'
      {% endfor %}
),

-- A person checked that this Overture place is the same facility as one OSM court group although no radius reaches it (seeds/place_venue_link.csv, ADR 0031).
seeded as (
    select l.place_id, c.venue_id,
           sqrt(power((p.lat - c.lat) * 110540, 2) + power((p.lon - c.lon) * cos(radians(p.lat)) * 111320, 2)) as distance_m
    from {{ ref('place_venue_link') }} l
    join places p on p.place_id = l.place_id
    join courts c on c.court_id = l.court_id
),

all_ruled as (
    select place_id, venue_id, distance_m, 'seed_link' as match_rule from seeded
    union all
    select place_id, venue_id, distance_m, match_rule from ruled where match_rule is not null
    union all
    select place_id, venue_id, distance_m, 'inside_facility' from in_footprint where distance_m <= {{ inside_radius }}
)

select place_id, venue_id, distance_m, match_rule
from (
    select *, row_number() over (
        partition by place_id
        order by case match_rule when 'seed_link' then 0 when 'distance' then 1 when 'same_name' then 2 when 'facility_name' then 3 else 4 end, distance_m, venue_id
    ) as rn
    from all_ruled
) x
where rn = 1

model.courtconnect.int_search_interest.name: int_search_interest
model.courtconnect.int_search_interest.description: Google Trends interest by metro on one scale (docs/search_interest_plan.md). Relative and sampled, not volumes or people. Las Vegas, from the Nevada query, is rescaled onto the California scale through Reno. `index_source` and `confidence` say how each value was made.
model.courtconnect.int_search_interest.raw_code:
-- Google Trends "interest by metro" on ONE scale (docs/search_interest_plan.md). Relative, sampled searches; not volumes, not people.
-- Each Trends query scales a sport to 100 at its top metro, and the California and Nevada queries have different tops. Reno is in both,
-- so Las Vegas (Nevada query only) is rescaled onto the California scale by Reno's ratio. No Reno data in either query = no Las Vegas index.
--   index_source : california_query | nevada_query_rescaled_via_reno | no_data
--   confidence   : ok (the five busiest sports) | thin (low-volume terms: Trends samples them, so values are noisy)
with raw as (
    select
        query_geo,
        metro_code,
        sport,
        term,
        query_set,
        exported_on,
        try_cast(index_value as double)  as index_value
    from {{ ref('search_interest') }}
),

ca as (
    select * from raw where query_geo = 'US-CA'
),

nv as (
    select * from raw where query_geo = 'US-NV'
),

reno_bridge as (
    select ca.sport, ca.index_value / nv.index_value as factor
    from ca
    join nv on nv.sport = ca.sport and nv.metro_code = ca.metro_code
    where ca.metro_code = 811 and ca.index_value > 0 and nv.index_value > 0
),

unioned as (
    select sport, term, metro_code, query_set, exported_on, index_value,
           case when index_value is null then 'no_data' else 'california_query' end as index_source
    from ca
    union all
    select nv.sport, nv.term, nv.metro_code, nv.query_set, nv.exported_on,
           round(nv.index_value * b.factor, 0)                                        as index_value,
           case when nv.index_value is null or b.factor is null then 'no_data' else 'nevada_query_rescaled_via_reno' end as index_source
    from nv
    left join reno_bridge b on b.sport = nv.sport
    where nv.metro_code <> 811
)

select
    u.metro_code,
    m.metro_name,
    u.sport,
    u.term,
    u.index_value,
    u.index_source,
    case when u.query_set = 'A' then 'ok' else 'thin' end as confidence,
    u.exported_on
from unioned u
join {{ ref('search_metros') }} m on m.metro_code = u.metro_code

model.courtconnect.int_venue_display_nam.name: int_venue_display_name
model.courtconnect.int_venue_display_nam.description: Display name for inferred-name venues that share lower(name) + city with another venue: "<name> (<direction> courts, <N courts>[, #k])". Direction is the 8-point compass bearing from the group centroid ("central" within 100 m), N is the mapped court count. Computed from position and court count, not from a source, so name quality stays inferred. venue_id is never changed.
model.courtconnect.int_venue_display_nam.raw_code:
-- Display name for every venue. Pins whose name is only INFERRED from an enclosing campus, club or park (name_source 'enclosing_feature')
-- often share one name inside a city (six "UC San Diego" pins in La Jolla). When 2+ venues share lower(name) + city, each inferred one gets
-- a computed suffix: "<direction from the group's centroid> courts, <N courts>", e.g. "UC San Diego (north courts, 6 courts)".
--   direction : 8-point compass of the venue relative to the centroid of ALL same-name venues in that city; "central" within 100 m of it
--   count     : dim_venue.court_records (mapped courts, all sports), else "court count unknown"
--   still equal after that (same direction and count): ", #1", ", #2"... by distance from the centroid, then venue_id
-- The suffix comes from position and court count, NOT from a source, so the name stays inferred (name_source / name quality unchanged).
-- Named by a person or a source (court_name, operator, manual, places_directory) are left alone: chain branches such as LA Fitness are
-- real separate places. venue_id is untouched. City is the final city (int_venue_address), so this cannot live in dim_venue.
with v as (
    select d.venue_id, d.venue_name, d.name_source, d.lat, d.lon, d.court_records, lower(a.city) as city_key
    from {{ ref('dim_venue') }} d
    join {{ ref('int_venue_address') }} a on a.venue_id = d.venue_id
    where d.name_source <> 'unnamed' and d.venue_name is not null and a.city is not null and d.lat is not null and d.lon is not null
),

grp as (
    select *,
           count(*) over (partition by lower(venue_name), city_key) as group_size,
           avg(lat) over (partition by lower(venue_name), city_key) as clat,
           avg(lon) over (partition by lower(venue_name), city_key) as clon
    from v
),

pos as (
    select *,
           (lon - clon) * cos(radians(clat)) * 111320            as dx,
           (lat - clat) * 110540                                 as dy
    from grp
    where group_size > 1 and name_source = 'enclosing_feature'
),

dir as (
    select *,
           sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)                               as dist_m,
           case
               when sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy) < 100 then 'central'
               else (['north', 'northeast', 'east', 'southeast', 'south', 'southwest', 'west', 'northwest'])[
                        1 + cast(floor(((degrees(atan2(dx, dy)) + 360 + 22.5) % 360) / 45) as integer) % 8]
           end                                                   as direction,
           case when court_records > 0
                then cast(court_records as varchar) || case when court_records = 1 then ' court' else ' courts' end
                else 'court count unknown' end                   as count_label
    from pos
),

ranked as (
    select *,
           count(*) over (partition by lower(venue_name), city_key, direction, count_label) as same_label,
           row_number() over (partition by lower(venue_name), city_key, direction, count_label order by dist_m, venue_id) as ord
    from dir
)

select
    venue_id,
    venue_name || ' (' || direction || ' courts, ' || count_label
                || case when same_label > 1 then ', #' || cast(ord as varchar) else '' end || ')'   as display_name
from ranked

model.courtconnect.int_venue_pairs_15mi.name: int_venue_pairs_15mi
model.courtconnect.int_venue_pairs_15mi.description: Helper for the market marts: every (venue, sport at another venue) pair within 15 miles, straight-line. Only sports a venue is directly listed for count, so "also played" inferences do not inflate the numbers.
model.courtconnect.int_venue_pairs_15mi.raw_code:
-- Helper for the market marts: every (venue, sport at ANOTHER venue) pair within 15 miles, straight-line (not drive time).
-- Only sports a venue is directly listed for count: sports that exist only as an "also played" inference (sport_also_played, e.g. Frescotennis
-- on every tennis court) would inflate every number, so they are left out here.
with vs as (
    select distinct venue_id, sport_name, lat, lon
    from {{ ref('mart_venue_finder') }}
    where lat is not null
      and lon is not null
      and sport_name not in (select trim(also_sport) from {{ ref('sport_also_played') }})
),

venues as (
    select venue_id, any_value(lat) as lat, any_value(lon) as lon
    from vs
    group by 1
)

select
    a.venue_id,
    b.venue_id  as other_venue_id,
    b.sport_name,
    {{ distance_mi('a.lat', 'a.lon', 'b.lat', 'b.lon') }}  as dist_mi
from venues a
join vs b
  on b.venue_id <> a.venue_id
 and abs(b.lat - a.lat) < 0.22      -- 15 miles is ~0.217 degrees of latitude: cheap prefilter before the exact distance
 and abs(b.lon - a.lon) < 0.30      -- ~0.28 degrees of longitude at 40N
where {{ distance_mi('a.lat', 'a.lon', 'b.lat', 'b.lon') }} <= 15

model.courtconnect.int_wall_clusters.name: int_wall_clusters
model.courtconnect.int_wall_clusters.description: Groups OSM walls of the same type that stand side by side (a school's row of handball courts) into one map pin, using the same label-propagation idea as int_court_clusters. Hand-added walls are never grouped. assert_wall_clusters_converged proves enough passes ran.
model.courtconnect.int_wall_clusters.raw_code:
-- Groups OpenStreetMap walls that stand side by side (a school's row of handball courts) into one map pin: connected
-- components of the "same wall type, within `wall_group_radius_m`" graph, labelled the same way as int_court_clusters
-- (each wall adopts the smallest key among its neighbours on every pass). Hand-added walls are never grouped: each one
-- was reported on its own. The wall set is small (under a thousand), so a plain self-join is enough here.
-- `changed_in_last_pass` lets assert_wall_clusters_converged prove we ran enough passes.
{% set passes = 8 %}

with walls as (
    select wall_key, wall_type, lat, lon from {{ ref('dim_wall') }}
),

pairs as (
    select a.wall_key as wall_a, b.wall_key as wall_b
    from walls a
    join walls b
        on b.wall_key <> a.wall_key
       and b.wall_type = a.wall_type
       and abs(b.lat - a.lat) < 0.01
    where a.wall_key like 'osm-%' and b.wall_key like 'osm-%'
      and sqrt(
              power((a.lat - b.lat) * 110540, 2)
            + power((a.lon - b.lon) * cos(radians(a.lat)) * 111320, 2)
          ) <= {{ var('wall_group_radius_m') }}
),

l0 as (
    select wall_key, wall_key as label from walls
)
{% for i in range(1, passes + 1) %}
, l{{ i }} as (
    select
        c.wall_key,
        least(c.label, coalesce(min(n.label), c.label)) as label
    from l{{ i - 1 }} c
    left join pairs p on p.wall_a = c.wall_key
    left join l{{ i - 1 }} n on n.wall_key = p.wall_b
    group by c.wall_key, c.label
)
{% endfor %}

select
    a.wall_key,
    a.label                       as wall_group,
    (a.label <> b.label)          as changed_in_last_pass
from l{{ passes }} a
join l{{ passes - 1 }} b on b.wall_key = a.wall_key

model.courtconnect.mart_court_finder.name: mart_court_finder
model.courtconnect.mart_court_finder.description: One row per (court, sport) with everything a player needs (surface, lighting, access, court count). What the app uses to draw individual courts.
model.courtconnect.mart_court_finder.raw_code:
-- What the app queries: one row per (court, sport) with everything a player needs.
select
    c.court_id,
    c.court_name,
    s.sport_name,
    c.lat,
    c.lon,
    c.surface_type,
    c.is_lit,
    c.access_type,
    c.is_free,
    c.courts_count
from {{ ref('dim_court') }} c
join {{ ref('bridge_court_sport') }} b on b.court_id = c.court_id
join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_id = b.sport_id

model.courtconnect.mart_market_gaps.name: mart_market_gaps
model.courtconnect.mart_market_gaps.description: One row per (city, sport) for every city with a mapped racket venue: venues in the city, venues within 15 miles of the city point, nearest venue, and a gap_status. INFERRED from known venues only (undercounts private clubs); the city point is the average of its venues, distances are straight-line. Read gap_status together with sport_coverage_status: for a sparse sport a gap may be missing data. No population yet.
model.courtconnect.mart_market_gaps.raw_code:
-- Where is a racket sport missing? One row per (city, sport) for every city with a mapped racket venue and every sport we list directly.
-- The city point is the average of its venues' coordinates (INFERRED, not the true center); distances are straight-line miles.
--   venues_in_city        : venues for the sport in the city
--   venues_within_15mi    : venues for the sport within 15 miles of that point
--   gap_status            : 'served' | 'nearby' (none in the city, one within 15 miles) | 'no_venue_within_15mi'
--   racket_venues_in_city : all directly listed racket venues in the city, a rough activity proxy (no population yet)
--   sport_coverage_status : from mart_sport_gaps; when the sport is sparse or unmapped, a gap may be missing data, not a real gap
with vs as (
    select
        venue_id,
        sport_name,
        upper(trim(any_value(city)))     as city_key,   -- Overture cities arrive in capitals ('IRVINE'), OSM in mixed case: match on the capitals
        any_value(city)                  as city_raw,
        any_value(region)                as region,
        any_value(lat)                   as lat,
        any_value(lon)                   as lon,
        max(courts_for_sport)            as courts,
        bool_or(is_confirmed_public)     as is_confirmed_public,
        bool_or(is_members_only)         as is_members_only
    from {{ ref('mart_venue_finder') }}
    where lat is not null
      and sport_name not in (select trim(also_sport) from {{ ref('sport_also_played') }})
    group by 1, 2
),

cities as (
    select
        region,
        city_key,
        coalesce(min(case when city_raw <> upper(city_raw) then city_raw end), min(city_raw))   as city,   -- prefer the mixed-case spelling for display
        avg(lat)                         as lat,
        avg(lon)                         as lon,
        count(distinct venue_id)         as racket_venues_in_city
    from vs
    where city_raw is not null
    group by 1, 2
),

sports as (
    select distinct sport_name from vs
),

in_city as (
    select
        region, city_key, sport_name,
        count(distinct venue_id)                                                  as venues_in_city,
        coalesce(sum(courts), 0)                                                  as courts_in_city,
        count(distinct case when is_confirmed_public then venue_id end)           as public_venues_in_city,
        count(distinct case when is_members_only then venue_id end)               as members_only_venues_in_city
    from vs
    where city_raw is not null
    group by 1, 2, 3
),

near as (
    select
        c.region, c.city_key, v.sport_name,
        count(distinct case when {{ distance_mi('c.lat', 'c.lon', 'v.lat', 'v.lon') }} <= 15 then v.venue_id end) as venues_within_15mi,
        min({{ distance_mi('c.lat', 'c.lon', 'v.lat', 'v.lon') }})                                              as nearest_mi
    from cities c
    join vs v on abs(v.lat - c.lat) < 1.5 and abs(v.lon - c.lon) < 2.0   -- ~100 miles: wide prefilter so far-off nearest venues are still found
    group by 1, 2, 3
)

select
    c.region,
    c.city,
    s.sport_name,
    c.racket_venues_in_city,
    coalesce(i.venues_in_city, 0)                                             as venues_in_city,
    coalesce(i.courts_in_city, 0)                                             as courts_in_city,
    coalesce(i.public_venues_in_city, 0)                                      as public_venues_in_city,
    coalesce(i.members_only_venues_in_city, 0)                                as members_only_venues_in_city,
    coalesce(n.venues_within_15mi, 0)                                         as venues_within_15mi,
    round(n.nearest_mi, 1)                                                    as nearest_mi,   -- null = none within ~100 miles
    case
        when coalesce(i.venues_in_city, 0) > 0         then 'served'
        when coalesce(n.venues_within_15mi, 0) > 0     then 'nearby'
        else 'no_venue_within_15mi'
    end                                                                       as gap_status,
    g.coverage_status                                                         as sport_coverage_status,
    'inferred'                                                                as confirmation
from cities c
cross join sports s
left join in_city i on i.region = c.region and i.city_key = c.city_key and i.sport_name = s.sport_name
left join near n    on n.region = c.region and n.city_key = c.city_key and n.sport_name = s.sport_name
left join {{ ref('mart_sport_gaps') }} g on g.sport_name = s.sport_name

model.courtconnect.mart_places_to_review.name: mart_places_to_review
model.courtconnect.mart_places_to_review.description: Places with weak sport evidence: a business name contains an ambiguous sport word ("Camino Real Tennis Center" is not Real Tennis). Never counted as a venue until a person confirms or rejects them in seeds/place_sport_overrides.csv.
model.courtconnect.mart_places_to_review.raw_code:
-- Weak evidence: a business name contains an ambiguous sport word ("Camino Real Tennis Center" looks like Real Tennis but is
-- not). Never counted as a venue until you confirm them: add a row  place_id,sport,confirm  (or  reject)  to
-- transform/seeds/place_sport_overrides.csv and rebuild.
select
    bp.place_id,
    s.sport_name,
    bp.matched_term,
    p.place_name,
    p.category,
    p.city,
    p.website,
    p.confidence,
    p.lat,
    p.lon
from {{ ref('bridge_place_sport') }} bp
join {{ ref('dim_place') }} p on p.place_id = bp.place_id
join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_id = bp.sport_id
where bp.evidence = 'weak'

model.courtconnect.mart_search_vs_covera.name: mart_search_vs_coverage
model.courtconnect.mart_search_vs_covera.description: One row per (Google Trends metro, sport): relative search interest next to the venues we have near that metro's anchor city. A planning signal for where to look for missing venues (gap_candidate); thin sports are noisy. Not exported to the app.
model.courtconnect.mart_search_vs_covera.raw_code:
-- Where do people search for a sport but find few pins? One row per (metro, sport). Planning signal only: it is not shown in the app.
-- interest_index is Google Trends relative search interest (100 = the metro with the most searches for that sport in CA + NV, sampled; docs/search_interest_plan.md).
-- Venues are assigned to the NEAREST metro anchor within 120 miles (our own approximation, not the Nielsen/Google metro boundaries).
--   gap_candidate : confidence 'ok', index >= 50 and 3 or fewer venues for the sport: a place to look for missing venues first, not proof of a gap
with metro as (
    select metro_code, metro_name, anchor_lat, anchor_lon from {{ ref('search_metros') }}
),

vs as (
    select venue_id, sport_name, any_value(lat) as lat, any_value(lon) as lon
    from {{ ref('mart_venue_finder') }}
    where lat is not null
      and sport_name not in (select trim(also_sport) from {{ ref('sport_also_played') }})
    group by 1, 2
),

nearest as (
    select venue_id, sport_name, metro_code
    from (
        select
            v.venue_id, v.sport_name, m.metro_code,
            row_number() over (partition by v.venue_id, v.sport_name
                               order by {{ distance_mi('m.anchor_lat', 'm.anchor_lon', 'v.lat', 'v.lon') }}) as rn,
            {{ distance_mi('m.anchor_lat', 'm.anchor_lon', 'v.lat', 'v.lon') }}                               as dist_mi
        from vs v
        cross join metro m
    )
    where rn = 1 and dist_mi <= 120
),

venues as (
    select metro_code, sport_name, count(distinct venue_id) as venues_found
    from nearest
    group by 1, 2
)

select
    i.metro_code,
    i.metro_name,
    i.sport                                                                       as sport_name,
    i.term                                                                        as search_term,
    i.index_value                                                                 as interest_index,
    i.index_source,
    i.confidence,
    coalesce(v.venues_found, 0)                                                   as venues_found,
    case when i.index_value is not null
         then rank() over (partition by i.sport order by i.index_value desc nulls last) end as interest_rank,
    coalesce(i.confidence = 'ok' and i.index_value >= 50 and coalesce(v.venues_found, 0) <= 3, false) as gap_candidate,
    i.exported_on
from {{ ref('int_search_interest') }} i
left join venues v on v.metro_code = i.metro_code and v.sport_name = i.sport

model.courtconnect.mart_social_events.name: mart_social_events
model.courtconnect.mart_social_events.description: Recurring social get-togethers (mixers, club nights, open play). Link-out only; age_focus and audience are organizer-stated, never inferred.
model.courtconnect.mart_social_events.raw_code:
-- Recurring social get-togethers to join, grouped by sport and city in the app. A discovery list: every row links out to the organizer.
-- `is_current` is as of the build date; the map app recomputes it in the browser so a stale deploy still hides ended series.
select
    e.series_id,
    e.series_name,
    e.sport_name,
    e.kind,
    e.organizer,
    e.venue_name,
    e.city,
    e.lat,
    e.lon,
    e.location_precision,
    e.schedule,
    e.last_listed_date,
    e.skill_level,
    e.audience,
    e.age_focus,
    e.courts,
    e.price_info,
    e.source_kind,
    e.info_url,
    e.signup_url,
    e.source_note,
    e.verified_on,
    (e.last_listed_date is null or e.last_listed_date >= current_date)   as is_current
from {{ ref('stg_social_events') }} e
join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_name = e.sport_name

model.courtconnect.mart_sport_gaps.name: mart_sport_gaps
model.courtconnect.mart_sport_gaps.description: One row per racket sport with an honest coverage status and the recommended next data source.
model.courtconnect.mart_sport_gaps.raw_code:
-- Every racket sport on the master sheet, with an honest status and what to do about it.
--   covered            : 5+ venues found
--   sparse             : 1-4 venues found
--   possible_only      : no confirmed venue, but some business names mention it (weak matches, review them)
--   tagged_none_found  : OpenStreetMap has a tag for it, but nothing is mapped in California or Nevada
--   not_found          : no OpenStreetMap tag and no place found: needs a club / governing-body directory
with tags as (
    select sport, count(*) as osm_tag_count, min(confidence) as worst_confidence
    from {{ ref('osm_sport_map') }}
    group by sport
),

cov as (
    select * from {{ ref('mart_sport_coverage') }}
)

select
    s.sport_name,
    s.popularity_class,
    s.governing_body,
    s.official_url,
    coalesce(t.osm_tag_count, 0) > 0                          as has_osm_tag,
    t.worst_confidence                                        as osm_mapping_confidence,
    coalesce(cov.venues_found, 0)                             as venues_found,
    coalesce(cov.osm_venues, 0)                               as osm_venues,
    coalesce(cov.places_venues, 0)                            as places_venues,
    coalesce(cov.courts_found, 0)                             as courts_found,
    coalesce(cov.weak_name_matches, 0)                        as weak_name_matches,
    case
        when coalesce(cov.venues_found, 0) >= 5               then 'covered'
        when coalesce(cov.venues_found, 0) >= 1               then 'sparse'
        when coalesce(cov.weak_name_matches, 0) > 0           then 'possible_only'
        when coalesce(t.osm_tag_count, 0) > 0                 then 'tagged_none_found'
        else 'not_found'
    end                                                       as coverage_status,
    case
        when coalesce(cov.venues_found, 0) >= 5               then 'OpenStreetMap and the places directory are sufficient; enrich names and hours'
        when coalesce(cov.venues_found, 0) >= 1               then 'Supplement with club directories and the governing-body list'
        when coalesce(cov.weak_name_matches, 0) > 0           then 'Review the weak name matches in mart_places_to_review'
        when coalesce(t.osm_tag_count, 0) > 0                 then 'Nothing mapped in California or Nevada yet: check governing-body and club directories'
        else 'Governing-body or club directory, Meetup groups; Google place IDs for live lookup'
    end                                                       as recommended_next_source
from {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s
left join tags t on t.sport = s.sport_name
left join cov on cov.sport_name = s.sport_name
where s.sport_family like 'Racket%'

model.courtconnect.mart_sport_surface_co.name: mart_sport_surface_coverage
model.courtconnect.mart_sport_surface_co.description: Courts and venues per sport, split by playing surface and indoor or outdoor setting. Answers "any indoor clay in California?".
model.courtconnect.mart_sport_surface_co.raw_code:
-- Courts and venues per sport, split by playing surface and indoor/outdoor setting.
-- Answers "where can I play padel on sand?", "any indoor clay in California?", "grass courts?".
select
    s.sport_name,
    c.surface_type,
    c.setting,
    count(distinct c.court_id)                                as courts,
    count(distinct c.venue_id)                                as venues,
    count(distinct case when c.access_type = 'public' then c.venue_id end) as public_venues
from {{ ref('bridge_court_sport') }} b
join {{ ref('dim_court') }} c on c.court_id = b.court_id
join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_id = b.sport_id
where c.record_kind = 'court'
group by 1, 2, 3

model.courtconnect.mart_venue_actions.name: mart_venue_actions
model.courtconnect.mart_venue_actions.description: Link-outs for a venue (open play, clinics, tournaments, social accounts). RacketConnect takes no bookings or payments; every row links to the provider's own page and carries verified_on and evidence (ADR 0007, 0009).

action_type.name: action_type
action_type.description: open_play, drop_in, clinic, league, tournament, social, club_page and so on.

model.courtconnect.mart_venue_actions.raw_code:
-- Things to do at each venue, with the provider's link. Link-outs only: the provider (not RacketConnect) takes any registration or payment.
select
    a.action_key,
    a.venue_id,
    coalesce(dn.display_name, v.venue_name) as venue_name,
    v.city,
    a.action_type,
    a.title,
    a.provider,
    a.url,
    a.price_info,
    a.start_date,
    a.end_date,
    (a.end_date is null or a.end_date >= current_date)        as is_current,
    a.evidence,
    a.verified_on
from {{ ref('stg_venue_actions') }} a
join {{ ref('dim_venue') }} v on v.venue_id = a.venue_id
left join {{ ref('int_venue_display_name') }} dn on dn.venue_id = a.venue_id

model.courtconnect.mart_venue_leads.name: mart_venue_leads
model.courtconnect.mart_venue_leads.description: Open research leads (claims we have not confirmed, such as whether a club is members only). Leads are never shown as facts on the map.
model.courtconnect.mart_venue_leads.raw_code:
-- To-do list for sleuthing: every lead that still needs work, oldest first. Closed leads (confirmed / resolved / rejected) drop off.
select
    lead_id,
    lead_name,
    city,
    sport_name,
    claim,
    source_type,
    source_url,
    status,
    next_step,
    noted_on,
    notes,
    directories_seen
from {{ ref('stg_venue_leads') }}
where status in ('new', 'needs_location', 'needs_visit')

model.courtconnect.mart_venue_nearby_spo.name: mart_venue_nearby_sports
model.courtconnect.mart_venue_nearby_spo.description: Per venue, the sports it is not listed for that other venues offer within 15 miles (count, nearest). Absence of a row means none within 15 miles in our data. INFERRED.
model.courtconnect.mart_venue_nearby_spo.raw_code:
-- "Try another sport": for each venue, the racket sports it is NOT listed for that are available at other venues within 15 miles
-- (straight-line), with how many and the nearest one. A sport missing from a venue's rows has nothing within 15 miles in our data,
-- which can also mean the sport is under-mapped (see mart_sport_gaps). INFERRED.
select
    p.venue_id,
    p.sport_name,
    count(distinct p.other_venue_id)                                       as venues_within_15mi,
    count(distinct case when p.dist_mi <= 5 then p.other_venue_id end)     as venues_within_5mi,
    round(min(p.dist_mi), 2)                                               as nearest_mi,
    'inferred'                                                             as confirmation
from {{ ref('int_venue_pairs_15mi') }} p
where not exists (
    select 1
    from {{ ref('mart_venue_neighbors') }} n
    where n.venue_id = p.venue_id and n.sport_name = p.sport_name
)
group by 1, 2

model.courtconnect.mart_venue_neighbors.name: mart_venue_neighbors
model.courtconnect.mart_venue_neighbors.description: Per (venue, directly listed sport), how many other venues with the same sport are within 5 and 15 miles (straight-line). INFERRED; known venues only.
model.courtconnect.mart_venue_neighbors.raw_code:
-- Competition around each venue, per sport the venue is listed for: how many OTHER venues with the same sport sit within 5 and 15 miles
-- (straight-line). Known venues only, so it undercounts private clubs; INFERRED, not a market study. Null nearest_same_sport_mi = none within 15 miles.
with vs as (
    select
        venue_id,
        sport_name,
        any_value(venue_name)   as venue_name,
        any_value(city)         as city,
        any_value(region)       as region,
        max(courts_for_sport)   as courts_for_sport
    from {{ ref('mart_venue_finder') }}
    where lat is not null
      and sport_name not in (select trim(also_sport) from {{ ref('sport_also_played') }})
    group by 1, 2
)

select
    vs.venue_id,
    vs.venue_name,
    vs.city,
    vs.region,
    vs.sport_name,
    vs.courts_for_sport,
    count(distinct case when p.dist_mi <= 5 then p.other_venue_id end)    as same_sport_venues_5mi,
    count(distinct p.other_venue_id)                                      as same_sport_venues_15mi,
    round(min(p.dist_mi), 2)                                              as nearest_same_sport_mi,
    'inferred'                                                            as confirmation
from vs
left join {{ ref('int_venue_pairs_15mi') }} p
  on p.venue_id = vs.venue_id and p.sport_name = vs.sport_name
group by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6

model.courtconnect.mart_wall_pins.name: mart_wall_pins
model.courtconnect.mart_wall_pins.description: One row per hitting-wall map pin (the app's walls). OSM walls of the same type within `wall_group_radius_m` of each other (a row of handball courts at a school) share one pin at their centre; `wall_count` says how many walls stand there.
model.courtconnect.mart_wall_pins.raw_code:
-- One row per hitting-wall map pin (what the app exports). Walls grouped in int_wall_clusters share a pin at their
-- centre; `wall_count` says how many walls stand there. Flags that differ inside a group become NULL (unknown), never a
-- guess. The name is a real OSM name when any wall in the group has one, else the generic default.
with walls as (
    select w.*, c.wall_group
    from {{ ref('dim_wall') }} w
    join {{ ref('int_wall_clusters') }} c on c.wall_key = w.wall_key
),

grouped as (
    select
        wall_group,
        count(*)                                                                                   as wall_count,
        coalesce(min(case when wall_name <> 'Handball / wall court' then wall_name end), min(wall_name)) as wall_name,
        coalesce(min(nullif(city, '')), '')                                                        as city,
        min(region)                                                                                as region,
        avg(lat)                                                                                   as lat,
        avg(lon)                                                                                   as lon,
        min(location_precision)                                                                    as location_precision,
        min(wall_type)                                                                             as wall_type,
        max(case when sports_suited like '%Handball%' then 1 else 0 end)                           as s_handball,
        max(case when sports_suited like '%Racquetball%' then 1 else 0 end)                        as s_racquetball,
        max(case when sports_suited like '%Tennis%' then 1 else 0 end)                             as s_tennis,
        max(case when sports_suited like '%Squash%' then 1 else 0 end)                             as s_squash,
        max(case when sports_suited like '%Pickleball%' then 1 else 0 end)                         as s_pickleball,
        min(sports_suited)                                                                         as first_sports,
        min(near_venue_name)                                                                       as near_venue_name,
        case when count(distinct surface) = 1 and count(surface) = count(*) then min(surface) end  as surface,
        case when count(is_lit) = count(*) then
             case when min(case when is_lit then 1 else 0 end) = 1 then true
                  when max(case when is_lit then 1 else 0 end) = 0 then false end end              as is_lit,
        case when count(free_to_use) = count(*) then
             case when min(case when free_to_use then 1 else 0 end) = 1 then true
                  when max(case when free_to_use then 1 else 0 end) = 0 then false end end         as free_to_use,
        case when count(distinct access) = 1 and count(access) = count(*) then min(access) end     as access,
        min(confirmation)                                                                          as confirmation,
        max(reported_on)                                                                           as reported_on,
        min(evidence)                                                                              as first_evidence
    from walls
    group by wall_group
)

select
    wall_group                                                                                     as wall_key,
    wall_count,
    wall_name,
    city,
    region,
    lat,
    lon,
    location_precision,
    wall_type,
    -- one wall keeps its own list as written; a group gets the union, in the same order stg_osm_walls writes it
    case when wall_count = 1 then first_sports
         else concat_ws(';',
              case when s_handball = 1 then 'Handball' end,
              case when s_racquetball = 1 then 'Racquetball' end,
              case when s_tennis = 1 then 'Tennis' end,
              case when s_squash = 1 then 'Squash' end,
              case when s_pickleball = 1 then 'Pickleball' end) end                                as sports_suited,
    near_venue_name,
    surface,
    is_lit,
    free_to_use,
    access,
    confirmation,
    reported_on,
    case when wall_count = 1 then first_evidence
         else cast(wall_count as varchar) || ' walls mapped side by side in OpenStreetMap (within '
              || '{{ var("wall_group_radius_m") }} m); the pin is their centre. One of them: ' || first_evidence end as evidence
from grouped

model.courtconnect.mart_watch_events.name: mart_watch_events
model.courtconnect.mart_watch_events.description: Events to watch (pro and amateur tournaments, dome screenings). Link-out only, with date_status and location_precision saying how certain the data is (ADR 0006).
model.courtconnect.mart_watch_events.raw_code:
-- Events to go and watch, soonest first. A discovery list: every row links out to the organizer.
-- `is_upcoming` is as of the build date; the map app recomputes it in the browser so a stale deploy still hides past events.
select
    e.event_id,
    e.event_name,
    e.sport_name,
    e.level,
    e.watch_format,
    e.venue_name,
    e.city,
    e.lat,
    e.lon,
    e.location_precision,
    e.start_date,
    e.end_date,
    e.date_status,
    e.ticket_info,
    e.info_url,
    e.tickets_url,
    e.source_note,
    e.verified_on,
    (e.end_date is null or e.end_date >= current_date)        as is_upcoming
from {{ ref('stg_watch_events') }} e
join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_name = e.sport_name

model.courtconnect.mart_website_quality.name: mart_website_quality
model.courtconnect.mart_website_quality.description: Dead-website rate by source and Overture confidence band.
model.courtconnect.mart_website_quality.raw_code:
-- How trustworthy are the websites we hold? One row per source and confidence band.
-- Answers: does Overture's confidence score predict a dead website? (It does not.)
-- 'dead' = the domain no longer exists (DNS). 'unknown' checks are excluded from the dead rate.
with all_sites as (
    select
        'overture'                                            as source,
        case
            when confidence >= 0.9 then 'confidence 0.9-1.0'
            when confidence >= 0.5 then 'confidence 0.5-0.9'
            else 'confidence below 0.5'
        end                                                   as band,
        website_status
    from {{ ref('dim_place') }}
    where website is not null

    union all

    select 'osm', 'all', {{ website_status('c.website', 'w.status') }}
    from {{ ref('dim_court') }} c
    left join {{ ref('stg_website_checks') }} w on w.domain = {{ website_domain('c.website') }}
    where c.website is not null

    union all

    select 'manual', 'all', {{ website_status('m.website', 'w.status') }}
    from {{ ref('stg_manual_venues') }} m
    left join {{ ref('stg_website_checks') }} w on w.domain = {{ website_domain('m.website') }}
    where m.website is not null
)

select
    source,
    band,
    count(*)                                                  as listings_with_website,
    sum(case when website_status in ('ok', 'dead') then 1 else 0 end)  as checked,
    sum(case when website_status = 'dead' then 1 else 0 end)           as dead,
    sum(case when website_status = 'unknown' then 1 else 0 end)        as inconclusive,
    sum(case when website_status = 'unchecked' then 1 else 0 end)      as not_yet_checked,
    case when sum(case when website_status in ('ok', 'dead') then 1 else 0 end) = 0 then null
         else round(100.0 * sum(case when website_status = 'dead' then 1 else 0 end)
                    / sum(case when website_status in ('ok', 'dead') then 1 else 0 end), 1) end as pct_dead
from all_sites
group by 1, 2

model.courtconnect.stg_google_place_ids.name: stg_google_place_ids
model.courtconnect.stg_google_place_ids.description: Google place IDs for our venues, the only Google Places content the terms allow storing. Dormant: empty until ingestion/google_place_ids.py is run with an API key, which the project does not do for now (ADR 0005).
model.courtconnect.stg_google_place_ids.raw_code:
-- Google place IDs for our venues. Place IDs are the only Google Places content Google lets you store
-- (ingestion/google_place_ids.py stores nothing else). Empty until someone runs that script with an API key.
select
    venue_id,
    google_place_id,
    resolved_at
from {{ source('raw', 'google_place_ids') }}
where venue_id is not null and google_place_id is not null

model.courtconnect.stg_manual_venues.name: stg_manual_venues
model.courtconnect.stg_manual_venues.description: Venues no data source knows about, added by hand in seeds/manual_venues.csv, one row per (venue, sport). `evidence` says how well each entry is backed up; `access` is public, unknown or private.
model.courtconnect.stg_manual_venues.raw_code:
-- Venues no data source knows about, added by hand (transform/seeds/manual_venues.csv).
-- One row per (venue, sport). `evidence` says how well each entry is backed up; `access` is public / unknown / private.
select
    md5('manual/' || trim(venue_key))                         as venue_id,
    trim(venue_key)                                           as venue_key,
    trim(venue_name)                                          as venue_name,
    trim(sport)                                               as sport_name,
    nullif(trim(city), '')                                    as city,
    cast(lat as double)                                       as lat,
    cast(lon as double)                                       as lon,
    nullif(trim(location_precision), '')                      as location_precision,
    nullif(trim(website), '')                                 as website,
    lower(trim(surface_type))                                 as surface_type,
    lower(trim(setting))                                      as setting,
    nullif(trim(offerings), '')                               as offerings,
    try_cast(nullif(trim(courts), '') as integer)             as courts_count,
    lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(access), ''), 'unknown'))      as access_type,
    nullif(trim(rules), '')                                   as rules_note,
    lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(confirmation), ''), 'reported')) as confirmation_level,   -- visited | official | reported
    cast(nullif(trim(confirmed_on), '') as date)              as confirmed_on,
    nullif(trim(evidence), '')                                as evidence,
    {{ region_code('region') }}                               as region
from {{ ref('manual_venues') }}

model.courtconnect.stg_manual_walls.name: stg_manual_walls
model.courtconnect.stg_manual_walls.description: Hitting walls for solo practice (one-wall, three-wall, backboards) curated in seeds/manual_walls.csv. A wall is not a court, so it lives apart from venues. Blank is_lit or free_to_use means unknown, never "no".
model.courtconnect.stg_manual_walls.raw_code:
-- Hitting walls for solo practice (one-wall, three-wall, backboards): curated in seeds/manual_walls.csv. A wall is not a court,
-- so it lives apart from venues. Blank is_lit / free_to_use means unknown (never read as no).
select
    trim(wall_key)                                            as wall_key,
    md5('wall/' || trim(wall_key))                            as wall_id,
    trim(wall_name)                                           as wall_name,
    trim(city)                                                as city,
    cast(lat as double)                                       as lat,
    cast(lon as double)                                       as lon,
    trim(location_precision)                                  as location_precision,
    lower(trim(wall_type))                                    as wall_type,
    trim(sports_suited)                                       as sports_suited,
    nullif(trim(near_venue_name), '')                         as near_venue_name,
    nullif(lower(trim(surface)), '')                          as surface,
    case lower(trim(is_lit)) when 'yes' then true when 'no' then false end            as is_lit,
    case lower(trim(free_to_use)) when 'yes' then true when 'no' then false end      as free_to_use,
    nullif(lower(trim(access)), '')                           as access,
    lower(trim(confirmation))                                 as confirmation,
    cast(reported_on as date)                                 as reported_on,
    nullif(trim(evidence), '')                                as evidence,
    {{ region_code('region') }}                               as region
from {{ ref('manual_walls') }}

model.courtconnect.stg_osm_parents.name: stg_osm_parents
model.courtconnect.stg_osm_parents.description: Named areas (parks, schools, clubs, sports centres) with bounding boxes, grouped into a kind_group. Used to name unnamed courts.
model.courtconnect.stg_osm_parents.raw_code:
-- Named areas (parks, schools, clubs...) with bounding boxes, used to name unnamed courts.
select
    osm_type || '/' || cast(osm_id as varchar)                as parent_id,
    trim(name)                                                as parent_name,
    kind                                                      as osm_kind,
    case
        when kind in ('leisure=park', 'leisure=garden', 'leisure=recreation_ground')                  then 'park'
        when kind in ('leisure=sports_centre', 'leisure=stadium', 'leisure=fitness_centre', 'club=sport') then 'sports_facility'
        when kind in ('amenity=school', 'amenity=college', 'amenity=university')                      then 'school'
        when kind in ('amenity=community_centre', 'amenity=clubhouse')                                then 'community'
        else 'resort_or_other'
    end                                                       as kind_group,
    cast(minlat as double)                                    as minlat,
    cast(minlon as double)                                    as minlon,
    cast(maxlat as double)                                    as maxlat,
    cast(maxlon as double)                                    as maxlon,
    (cast(maxlat as double) - cast(minlat as double))
      * (cast(maxlon as double) - cast(minlon as double))     as bbox_area_deg2,
    -- the address mapped on the feature itself (addr:housenumber + addr:street), when someone tagged one
    case when nullif(trim(addr_housenumber), '') is not null and nullif(trim(addr_street), '') is not null
         then trim(addr_housenumber) || ' ' || trim(addr_street) end   as address_line,
    nullif(trim(addr_city), '')                               as addr_city
from {{ source('raw', 'osm_parents') }}
where name is not null and trim(name) <> ''

model.courtconnect.stg_osm_walls.name: stg_osm_walls
model.courtconnect.stg_osm_walls.description: Hitting walls mapped in OpenStreetMap (handball and wall courts, tennis backboards). OSM does not say how many walls a court has, so with no other source a handball or wallball court is assumed one-wall and labelled "assumed". Blank lit or fee means unknown.
model.courtconnect.stg_osm_walls.raw_code:
-- Hitting walls mapped in OpenStreetMap (handball and wall courts, tennis backboards and practice walls). The wall type is not
-- known from the tags: sport=american_handball is used for 1-wall, 3-wall and 4-wall courts alike, and OSM has no wall-count tag.
-- Owner decision 2026-10-22 (replaces 2026-10-14, when every one was called three-wall): with no public page or visit report
-- either way, a handball / wallball court is assumed ONE-wall (the app labels it "assumed"). A three_wall type needs a reported
-- or official source in manual_walls.csv, or an imagery read in osm_wall_overrides.csv (`inferred`, evidence + date). Backboard stays
-- 'backboard' when the name or tags say so.
-- Blank lit / fee means unknown (never read as no). The pin is the mapped feature, so the location is exact.
with base as (
select
    'osm-' || osm_type || '-' || cast(cast(osm_id as bigint) as varchar)                      as wall_key,
    md5('wall/osm-' || osm_type || '-' || cast(cast(osm_id as bigint) as varchar))            as wall_id,
    coalesce(nullif(trim(name), ''), 'Handball / wall court')                                 as wall_name,
    coalesce(nullif(trim(addr_city), ''), '')                                                 as city,
    cast(lat as double)                                                                       as lat,
    cast(lon as double)                                                                       as lon,
    'exact: mapped feature in OpenStreetMap'                                                  as location_precision,
    case when lower(coalesce(name, '')) like '%backboard%' or lower(coalesce(name, '')) like '%practice wall%'
              or lower(coalesce(name, '')) like '%hitting wall%' or tennis = 'hitting_wall' or leisure = 'practice_wall'
         then 'backboard'
         when lower(sport) like '%handball%' or lower(sport) like '%wallball%' then 'one_wall'
         else 'other' end                                                    as wall_type,
    concat_ws(';',
        case when lower(sport) like '%handball%' or lower(sport) like '%wallball%' then 'Handball' end,
        case when lower(sport) like '%racquetball%' then 'Racquetball' end,
        case when lower(sport) like '%tennis%' or tennis = 'hitting_wall' then 'Tennis' end,
        case when lower(sport) like '%squash%' then 'Squash' end,
        case when lower(sport) like '%pickleball%' then 'Pickleball' end)                     as sports_suited,
    cast(null as varchar)                                                                     as near_venue_name,
    nullif(lower(trim(surface)), '')                                                          as surface,
    case lower(trim(lit)) when 'yes' then true when 'no' then false end                       as is_lit,
    case lower(trim(fee)) when 'no' then true when 'yes' then false end                       as free_to_use,
    -- same vocabulary as stg_osm_courts.access_type; anything unrecognised stays NULL (not known)
    case lower(trim(access))
        when 'yes' then 'public'
        when 'public' then 'public'
        when 'permissive' then 'public'
        when 'customers' then 'customers'
        when 'private' then 'private'
        when 'no' then 'private'
        when 'members' then 'members'
    end                                                                                       as access,
    'tagged'                                                                                  as confirmation,
    cast(extracted_at as date)                                                                as reported_on,
