    'OpenStreetMap ' || osm_type || ' ' || cast(cast(osm_id as bigint) as varchar) || ', tagged sport=' || coalesce(sport, 'n/a')
        || '. Only the tags are known: the number of walls (assumed one), condition and whether it is open to the public were not checked.'      as evidence,
    {{ region_code('region') }}                                                               as region
from {{ source('raw', 'osm_walls') }}
)

select
    b.wall_key, b.wall_id, b.wall_name, b.city, b.lat, b.lon, b.location_precision,
    coalesce(o.wall_type, b.wall_type)                   as wall_type,
    b.sports_suited, b.near_venue_name, b.surface, b.is_lit, b.free_to_use, b.access,
    coalesce(o.confirmation, b.confirmation)             as confirmation,
    coalesce(cast(o.verified_on as date), b.reported_on) as reported_on,
    coalesce(o.evidence, b.evidence)                     as evidence,
    b.region
from base b
left join {{ ref('osm_wall_overrides') }} o on o.wall_key = b.wall_key

model.courtconnect.stg_overture_addresse.name: stg_overture_addresses
model.courtconnect.stg_overture_addresse.description: Overture address points near map pins (house number + street), used only to fill pins that have no address.
model.courtconnect.stg_overture_addresse.raw_code:
-- Overture Maps address points that sit near a map pin (CDLA-Permissive; NOTICE.md). Not the whole state: the extract keeps
-- only the points within ~440 m of a pin (ingestion/extract_overture_addresses.py). Used to fill pins with no street address.
select
    address_id,
    trim(concat_ws(' ', cast(house_number as varchar), cast(street as varchar))) as address_line,
    nullif(trim(cast(city as varchar)), '')                   as city,
    nullif(trim(cast(postcode as varchar)), '')               as postcode,
    cast(lat as double)                                       as lat,
    cast(lon as double)                                       as lon
from {{ source('raw', 'overture_addresses') }}
where lat is not null and lon is not null
  and nullif(trim(cast(house_number as varchar)), '') is not null
  and nullif(trim(cast(street as varchar)), '') is not null

model.courtconnect.stg_overture_places.name: stg_overture_places
model.courtconnect.stg_overture_places.description: Racket-related places from Overture Maps, closed businesses removed.
model.courtconnect.stg_overture_places.raw_code:
-- Racket-related places from Overture Maps (businesses, clubs, venues). Licensed CDLA-Permissive-2.0 / Apache-2.0 / CC0,
-- so unlike Google Places content it can be stored and republished with attribution (NOTICE.md).
select
    place_id,
    trim(name)                                                as place_name,
    {{ normalize_name('name') }}                              as name_norm,
    category,
    top_category,
    sub_category,
    cast(lat as double)                                       as lat,
    cast(lon as double)                                       as lon,
    cast(confidence as double)                                as confidence,
    nullif(trim(website), '')                                 as website,
    nullif(trim(phone), '')                                   as phone,
    nullif(trim(address), '')                                 as address_line,
    nullif(trim(city), '')                                    as city,
    nullif(trim(postcode), '')                                as postcode,
    license,
    source_dataset,
    release,
    {{ region_code('region') }}                               as region   -- from the border polygon at extract time (ADR 0014), not the address
from {{ source('raw', 'overture_places') }}
where lat is not null and lon is not null
  and coalesce(lower(operating_status), 'open') not in ('closed', 'permanently_closed')
  -- seeds/closed_places.csv: places that Overture still lists as open but that no longer exist (owner or public-page evidence)
  and place_id not in (select place_id from {{ ref('closed_places') }})

model.courtconnect.stg_social_events.name: stg_social_events
model.courtconnect.stg_social_events.description: Recurring social get-togethers (mixers, club nights, open play), one row per series and not per date, each linking to the organizer's own page. RacketConnect takes no signups or payments.
model.courtconnect.stg_social_events.raw_code:
-- Recurring social get-togethers (mixers, club nights, open play, social nights): curated in seeds/social_events.csv, one row per SERIES
-- (not per date, so rows do not go stale each week), each with a link to the organizer's own page. RacketConnect takes no signups or payments.
select
    trim(series_key)                                          as series_key,
    md5('social/' || trim(series_key))                        as series_id,
    trim(series_name)                                         as series_name,
    trim(sport)                                               as sport_name,
    lower(trim(kind))                                         as kind,
    trim(organizer)                                           as organizer,
    trim(venue_name)                                          as venue_name,
    trim(city)                                                as city,
    cast(lat as double)                                       as lat,
    cast(lon as double)                                       as lon,
    trim(location_precision)                                  as location_precision,
    trim(schedule)                                            as schedule,
    cast(nullif(trim(last_listed_date), '') as date)          as last_listed_date,
    nullif(trim(skill_level), '')                             as skill_level,
    lower(nullif(trim(audience), ''))                         as audience,
    lower(nullif(trim(age_focus), ''))                        as age_focus,
    cast(nullif(trim(courts), '') as integer)                 as courts,
    nullif(trim(price_info), '')                              as price_info,
    lower(trim(source_kind))                                  as source_kind,
    nullif(trim(info_url), '')                                as info_url,
    nullif(trim(signup_url), '')                              as signup_url,
    nullif(trim(source_note), '')                             as source_note,
    cast(verified_on as date)                                 as verified_on
from {{ ref('social_events') }}

model.courtconnect.stg_sports.name: stg_sports
model.courtconnect.stg_sports.description: Cleaned sports reference data (typos fixed, text parsed into typed columns, de-duplicated).
model.courtconnect.stg_sports.raw_code:
-- Cleans the hand-maintained sports spreadsheet: fixes typos, parses messy
-- text (ranges, mixed units) into typed columns, and removes duplicates.
with src as (
    select * from {{ ref('all_racquet') }}
),

cleaned as (
    select
        md5(lower(trim(sport)))                               as sport_id,
        trim(sport)                                           as sport_name,
        trim(sport_type)                                      as sport_family,
        trim(popularity_class)                                as popularity_class,
        nullif(trim(org), '')                                 as governing_body,
        trim(active_loc)                                      as active_loc_raw,

        -- players: '2-4' -> 2/4, '2+' -> 2/null(open ended), '18' -> 18/18
        try_cast({{ regex_extract('players', '^([0-9]+)') }} as integer) as players_min,
        case
            when players like '%+' then null
            else try_cast(coalesce({{ regex_extract('players', '-([0-9]+)$') }}, {{ regex_extract('players', '^([0-9]+)$') }}) as integer)
        end                                                   as players_max,

        -- court: '44x20' (or '118.1×32.8') -> 44 x 20 ft. Anything else (blocks, circumference, 'user descretion') stays null.
        try_cast({{ regex_extract('court_dim', '^([0-9.]+)[x×][0-9.]+$') }} as double) as court_length_ft,
        try_cast({{ regex_extract('court_dim', '^[0-9.]+[x×]([0-9.]+)$') }} as double) as court_width_ft,

        lower(coalesce(court_surface, ''))                    as surface_lc,
        nullif(trim(base_gear), '')                           as base_gear,
        nullif(trim(net_type), '')                            as net_type,
        {{ to_inches('net_ht') }}                             as net_height_in,
        -- '5ft 7in / 5ft 11in' lists two heights (e.g. women / men): the first stays in net_height_in, the second goes here
        {{ to_inches("nullif(trim(split_part(net_ht, '/', 2)), '')") }} as net_height_alt_in,
        upper(trim(gear_avail_ao)) = 'Y'                      as gear_on_amazon_or_online,

        -- typo-proof: 'Competitve' / 'Non-Competitve' / blank
        case
            when lower(coalesce(competing, '')) like 'non%'   then 'Non-Competitive'
            when lower(coalesce(competing, '')) like 'comp%'  then 'Competitive'
            else 'Unknown'
        end                                                   as competitive_status,

        try_cast({{ regex_extract('year_origin', '^([0-9]{4})') }} as integer) as year_origin,
        nullif(trim(url), '')                                 as official_url,
        lower(coalesce(active_loc, ''))                       as loc_lc
    from src
    where sport is not null
),

deduped as (
    select *, row_number() over (partition by sport_id order by sport_name) as rn
    from cleaned
)

select * exclude (rn) from deduped where rn = 1

model.courtconnect.stg_venue_actions.name: stg_venue_actions
model.courtconnect.stg_venue_actions.description: What you can do at a venue (join a league, take a clinic, find open play, book a lesson), with the provider's own link. Link-outs only (ADR 0006). A row points at a hand-added venue or an Overture place; `evidence` and `verified_on` say how we know.
model.courtconnect.stg_venue_actions.raw_code:
-- What you can DO at a venue, with the provider's own link: join a league, take a clinic, find open play, book a lesson.
-- Link-outs only (ADR 0006): RacketConnect books nothing. Each row says which platform runs it, where to go, and how we know.
-- A row points at a hand-added venue (venue_ref_type 'manual', venue_ref = venue_key) or an Overture place ('place', venue_ref = place_id).
select
    trim(a.action_key)                                        as action_key,
    coalesce(mm.effective_venue_id, p.venue_id)               as venue_id,
    lower(trim(a.action_type))                                as action_type,
    trim(a.title)                                             as title,
    lower(trim(a.provider))                                   as provider,
    trim(a.url)                                               as url,
    nullif(trim(a.price_info), '')                            as price_info,
    cast(nullif(trim(a.start_date), '') as date)              as start_date,
    cast(nullif(trim(a.end_date), '') as date)                as end_date,
    nullif(trim(a.evidence), '')                              as evidence,
    cast(a.verified_on as date)                               as verified_on
from {{ ref('venue_actions') }} a
left join {{ ref('int_manual_venue_match') }} mm on lower(trim(a.venue_ref_type)) = 'manual' and mm.venue_key = trim(a.venue_ref)
left join {{ ref('dim_place') }} p on lower(trim(a.venue_ref_type)) = 'place' and p.place_id = trim(a.venue_ref)

model.courtconnect.stg_venue_confirmatio.name: stg_venue_confirmations
model.courtconnect.stg_venue_confirmatio.description: One row per person, method (visited, official, reported) and day confirming a hand-added venue. Feeds the confirmation level.
model.courtconnect.stg_venue_confirmatio.raw_code:
-- Individual confirmations of hand-added venues (transform/seeds/venue_confirmations.csv). One row per person, method and day.
select
    trim(venue_key)                              as venue_key,
    lower(trim(confirmed_by))                    as confirmed_by,     -- GitHub handle
    lower(trim(method))                          as method,           -- visited | official | reported (word of mouth)
    cast(nullif(trim(confirmed_on), '') as date) as confirmed_on,
    nullif(trim(evidence), '')                   as evidence
from {{ ref('venue_confirmations') }}

model.courtconnect.stg_venue_leads.name: stg_venue_leads
model.courtconnect.stg_venue_leads.description: The sleuthing backlog: things reported but not yet located or confirmed. A lead is never shown as a pin; once confirmed it becomes a manual_venues row.
model.courtconnect.stg_venue_leads.raw_code:
-- The sleuthing backlog: things reported but not yet located or confirmed (seeds/venue_leads.csv).
-- A lead is NOT shown on the map. When it is confirmed it becomes a row in manual_venues (with a confirmation level) and
-- its status here becomes 'confirmed' or 'resolved'.
select
    trim(lead_id)                                             as lead_id,
    trim(name)                                                as lead_name,
    nullif(trim(city), '')                                    as city,
    trim(sport)                                               as sport_name,
    nullif(trim(claim), '')                                   as claim,
    lower(trim(source_type))                                  as source_type,
    nullif(trim(source_url), '')                              as source_url,
    lower(trim(status))                                       as status,
    nullif(trim(next_step), '')                               as next_step,
    cast(noted_on as date)                                    as noted_on,
    nullif(trim(notes), '')                                   as notes,
    cast(nullif(trim(directories_seen), '') as integer)       as directories_seen   -- public padel directories seen listing it (2026-10-17; not evidence)
from {{ ref('venue_leads') }}

model.courtconnect.stg_watch_events.name: stg_watch_events
model.courtconnect.stg_watch_events.description: Matches and tournaments people can go and watch, curated in seeds/watch_events.csv, each with a link to the organizer's own page. Nothing is sold or reserved; info_url and tickets_url are link-outs.
model.courtconnect.stg_watch_events.raw_code:
-- Matches and tournaments people can go and WATCH (not book): curated in seeds/watch_events.csv, each with a link to the
-- organizer's own page. We never sell or reserve anything; `info_url` / `tickets_url` are link-outs.
select
    trim(event_key)                                           as event_key,
    md5('event/' || trim(event_key))                          as event_id,
    trim(event_name)                                          as event_name,
    trim(sport)                                               as sport_name,
    lower(trim(level))                                        as level,
    lower(trim(watch_format))                                 as watch_format,
    trim(venue_name)                                          as venue_name,
    trim(city)                                                as city,
    cast(lat as double)                                       as lat,
    cast(lon as double)                                       as lon,
    trim(location_precision)                                  as location_precision,
    cast(nullif(trim(start_date), '') as date)                as start_date,
    cast(nullif(trim(end_date), '') as date)                  as end_date,
    lower(trim(date_status))                                  as date_status,
    nullif(trim(ticket_info), '')                             as ticket_info,
    nullif(trim(info_url), '')                                as info_url,
    nullif(trim(tickets_url), '')                             as tickets_url,
    nullif(trim(source_note), '')                             as source_note,
    cast(verified_on as date)                                 as verified_on
from {{ ref('watch_events') }}

model.courtconnect.stg_website_checks.name: stg_website_checks
model.courtconnect.stg_website_checks.description: Website domain checks (DNS only). 'dead' means the domain definitively does not exist; 'unknown' is inconclusive.
model.courtconnect.stg_website_checks.raw_code:
-- Does each listed website still exist? Two sources, hand overrides first:
--   1. seeds/website_overrides.csv: sites a person found to be parked, hijacked or the wrong business. DNS cannot see these
--      (a parked domain still resolves), so a human flag wins over the automatic result.
--   2. ingestion/check_websites.py: DNS-only check. status ok | dead (domain does not exist) | unknown (inconclusive, never treated as dead).
with overrides as (
    select
        lower(trim(domain))                                   as domain,
        lower(trim(status))                                   as status,
        cast(null as varchar)                                 as resolved_host,
        cast(verified_on as varchar)                          as checked_at
    from {{ ref('website_overrides') }}
),

checks as (
    select
        domain,
        status,
        nullif(resolved_host, '')                             as resolved_host,
        cast(checked_at as varchar)                           as checked_at
    from {{ source('raw', 'website_checks') }}
    where domain is not null
)

select * from overrides
union all
select * from checks where domain not in (select domain from overrides)

test.courtconnect.assert_all_racket_spor.name: assert_all_racket_sports_loaded

test.courtconnect.assert_category_sport_.name: assert_category_sport_not_contradicted_by_name
test.courtconnect.assert_category_sport_.raw_code:
-- An Overture tennis_court / tennis_stadium must not make a table tennis, padel or pickleball-only name a Tennis place
-- (bridge_place_sport drops a category sport when the name only names another distinctive sport). Add a place_sport_overrides
-- confirm instead if one of these really does have tennis courts.
select p.place_name
from {{ ref('dim_place') }} p
join {{ ref('bridge_place_sport') }} bp on bp.place_id = p.place_id and bp.match_type = 'category'
join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_id = bp.sport_id and s.sport_name = 'Tennis'
where p.place_name like '%Table Tennis%'
   or p.place_name like '%Padel%'
   or (p.place_name like '%Pickleball%' and p.place_name not like '%Tennis%')

test.courtconnect.assert_clusters_conver.name: assert_clusters_converged
test.courtconnect.assert_clusters_conver.raw_code:
-- Fails if any court's venue label was still changing on the final pass,
-- which would mean the clustering needs more passes (raise `passes` in int_court_clusters).
select court_id from {{ ref('int_court_clusters') }} where changed_in_last_pass

test.courtconnect.assert_confidence_scor.name: assert_confidence_score_bounds

test.courtconnect.assert_confidence_v2_n.name: assert_confidence_v2_not_above_v1
test.courtconnect.assert_confidence_v2_n.raw_code:
-- The sport penalty can only lower a score, and only by up to 15 points.
select venue_id, confidence_score_v1, confidence_score
from {{ ref('mart_venue_confidence') }}
where confidence_score > confidence_score_v1 or confidence_score_v1 - confidence_score > 15

test.courtconnect.assert_confirmed_venue.name: assert_confirmed_venues_have_evidence
test.courtconnect.assert_confirmed_venue.raw_code:
-- A hand-added venue marked visited or official must say how we know (evidence). A visited row also needs the date of the visit.
select venue_key, sport_name, 'confirmed without evidence' as problem
from {{ ref('stg_manual_venues') }}
where confirmation_level in ('visited', 'official') and evidence is null
union all
select venue_key, sport_name, 'visited without a date'
from {{ ref('stg_manual_venues') }}
where confirmation_level = 'visited' and confirmed_on is null

test.courtconnect.assert_courts_inside_r.name: assert_courts_inside_region

test.courtconnect.assert_every_court_has.name: assert_every_court_has_one_venue
test.courtconnect.assert_every_court_has.raw_code:
select court_id from {{ ref('dim_court') }} where venue_id is null
union all
select 'venue_court_total_mismatch'
where (select sum(court_records + facility_records) from {{ ref('dim_venue') }} where venue_source in ('osm', 'osm+places')) <> (select count(*) from {{ ref('dim_court') }})

test.courtconnect.assert_indoor_has_basi.name: assert_indoor_has_basis
test.courtconnect.assert_indoor_has_basi.raw_code:
-- has_indoor is only true/false when something backs it (indoor_basis); with no basis it must be null (unknown), never a default false.
select venue_id, has_indoor, indoor_basis
from {{ ref('dim_venue') }}
where (indoor_basis = 'unknown' and has_indoor is not null)
   or (indoor_basis <> 'unknown' and has_indoor is null)

test.courtconnect.assert_inferred_names_.name: assert_inferred_names_unique_in_city
test.courtconnect.assert_inferred_names_.raw_code:
-- Venues whose name is only inferred (name_source 'enclosing_feature') must not share a displayed name inside a city: where the raw name is
-- shared, int_venue_display_name adds a "(direction courts, N courts[, #k])" suffix. A row here is two such pins that still look identical.
select lower(venue_name) as venue_name, lower(city) as city, count(distinct venue_id) as venues
from {{ ref('mart_venue_finder') }}
where name_source = 'enclosing_feature' and city is not null
group by 1, 2
having count(distinct venue_id) > 1

test.courtconnect.assert_manual_venues_i.name: assert_manual_venues_inside_region

test.courtconnect.assert_market_marts_co.name: assert_market_marts_consistent
test.courtconnect.assert_market_marts_co.raw_code:
-- Internal consistency of the market marts: (venue, sport) is unique in mart_venue_neighbors, a sport "to try nearby" is never one the venue
-- already lists, and a city marked 'served' has at least one venue.
select 'duplicate_neighbor_row' as problem, venue_id || '|' || sport_name as detail
from {{ ref('mart_venue_neighbors') }}
group by venue_id, sport_name
having count(*) > 1

union all

select 'nearby_sport_also_listed_at_venue', n.venue_id || '|' || n.sport_name
from {{ ref('mart_venue_nearby_sports') }} n
join {{ ref('mart_venue_neighbors') }} v on v.venue_id = n.venue_id and v.sport_name = n.sport_name

union all

select 'served_without_venue', city || '|' || sport_name
from {{ ref('mart_market_gaps') }}
where gap_status = 'served' and venues_in_city = 0

test.courtconnect.assert_net_height_sane.name: assert_net_height_sane

test.courtconnect.assert_no_duplicate_ve.name: assert_no_duplicate_venues
test.courtconnect.assert_no_duplicate_ve.raw_code:
-- Guard against the same facility being listed twice (e.g. one school's courts as three pins, or two Overture listings of
-- one address). Two venues with the same name within 150 m fail the build; fix by merging (int_court_pairs / dim_place)
-- or, for hand-added venues, by an entry in manual_venue_matches / a name fix. Hand-added pairs are left to review.
{% set d %}sqrt(power((a.lat - b.lat) * 110540, 2) + power((a.lon - b.lon) * cos(radians(a.lat)) * 111320, 2)){% endset %}
select a.venue_id as venue_a, b.venue_id as venue_b, a.venue_name, round({{ d }}) as distance_m
from {{ ref('dim_venue') }} a
join {{ ref('dim_venue') }} b
  on a.venue_id < b.venue_id
 and lower(a.venue_name) = lower(b.venue_name)
 and abs(a.lat - b.lat) < 0.002 and abs(a.lon - b.lon) < 0.003
where {{ d }} <= 150
  and not (a.venue_source = 'manual' and b.venue_source = 'manual')
  and a.name_source <> 'unnamed' and b.name_source <> 'unnamed'

test.courtconnect.assert_no_osm_wall_bes.name: assert_no_osm_wall_beside_confirmed_court
test.courtconnect.assert_no_osm_wall_bes.raw_code:
-- Fails if an OSM wall pin still stands within `wall_group_radius_m` of a hand-added one-wall / three-wall court: the confirmed
-- court should be the only pin (see dim_wall).
select o.wall_key
from {{ ref('dim_wall') }} o
join {{ ref('dim_wall') }} m
    on m.wall_key not like 'osm-%'
   and m.wall_type in ('one_wall', 'three_wall', 'one_wall;three_wall')
   and abs(m.lat - o.lat) < 0.01
   and sqrt(
           power((m.lat - o.lat) * 110540, 2)
         + power((m.lon - o.lon) * cos(radians(m.lat)) * 111320, 2)
       ) <= {{ var('wall_group_radius_m') }}
where o.wall_key like 'osm-%'

test.courtconnect.assert_no_sheet_sport_.name: assert_no_sheet_sport_dropped
test.courtconnect.assert_no_sheet_sport_.raw_code:
-- Fails if any sport named on the sheet fails to reach dim_sport (e.g. lost in de-duplication or cleaning).
select s.sport
from {{ ref('all_racquet') }} s
left join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} d on d.sport_id = md5(lower(trim(s.sport)))
where trim(s.sport) <> '' and d.sport_id is null

test.courtconnect.assert_padel_has_suppo.name: assert_padel_has_supporting_signal
test.courtconnect.assert_padel_has_suppo.raw_code:
-- Guard rail from the 2026-10-17 padel audit: most OpenStreetMap `sport=padel` tags (aerial-imagery passes) and name-only matches were wrong
-- (pickleball, backyard courts, pop tennis). A Padel venue must rest on a person's evidence: a hand-added venue with a club or official page
-- (rung 1 confirmed) or an owner / community report (rung 2 reported). An OSM tag alone (rung 3-4), an Overture category (5) or a business-name
-- word (6) is not enough: confirm the club on its own page (manual_venues.csv or a place_sport_overrides confirm), correct the court with
-- osm_court_sport_overrides.csv, or reject it. Rows returned here are Padel venues with no such evidence.
select
    v.venue_name,
    v.city,
    e.best_rung_label
from {{ ref('mart_sport_evidence') }} e
join {{ ref('dim_venue') }} v on v.venue_id = e.venue_id
where e.sport_name = 'Padel'
  and e.best_rung > 2

test.courtconnect.assert_place_sport_pai.name: assert_place_sport_pairs_unique
test.courtconnect.assert_place_sport_pai.raw_code:
-- A place may be linked to a sport only once (the strongest evidence wins).
select place_id, sport_id, count(*) as n
from {{ ref('bridge_place_sport') }}
group by 1, 2
having count(*) > 1

test.courtconnect.assert_pop_tennis_has_.name: assert_pop_tennis_has_supporting_signal
test.courtconnect.assert_pop_tennis_has_.raw_code:
-- Pop Tennis / paddle tennis (open court, low net) gets mixed up with Padel (walled glass court) in OSM tags and names (padel audit, 2026-10-17).
-- Padel has its own stricter test (assert_padel_has_supporting_signal). A Pop Tennis row needs a direct signal that is not a derivation:
--   allowed: confirmed or reported by a person (rungs 1-2), an Overture category (5), or a business-name word (6, stays in the review queue);
--   a loose OSM tag (4) only while it is flagged needs_review. A high-confidence OSM tag (3) or a derived row (7) is never enough.
-- To clear a failure: confirm the place in manual_venues / place_sport_overrides, reject a wrong OSM tag in osm_court_sport_overrides
-- (or re-identify it with correct_sport), or lower the tag's confidence in osm_sport_map.
select v.venue_name, e.sport_name, e.best_rung_label
from {{ ref('mart_sport_evidence') }} e
join {{ ref('dim_venue') }} v on v.venue_id = e.venue_id
where e.sport_name = 'Pop Tennis'
  and (e.best_rung in (3, 7) or (e.best_rung >= 4 and not e.needs_review))

test.courtconnect.assert_reported_pins_m.name: assert_reported_pins_merged
test.courtconnect.assert_reported_pins_m.raw_code:
-- A community report on an existing map venue (ci/issue_to_pr.py) is written at that pin's coordinates and must merge onto it,
-- not onto a neighbouring venue and not as a pin of its own. Warn only: map ids change when venues re-cluster, so a hit means
-- "a reviewer should look", not "the data is wrong".
{{ config(severity='warn') }}
select m.venue_key, m.location_precision, mm.effective_venue_id
from {{ ref('stg_manual_venues') }} m
join {{ ref('int_manual_venue_match') }} mm on mm.venue_key = m.venue_key
where m.location_precision like 'pin: map id %'
  and (not mm.is_matched
       or substr(mm.effective_venue_id, 1, 10) <> substr(m.location_precision, 13, 10))

test.courtconnect.assert_search_interest.name: assert_search_interest_valid
test.courtconnect.assert_search_interest.raw_code:
-- Search interest seed (docs/search_interest_plan.md): index is 0-100 or blank, never a made-up 0 for "no data", and every sport is a real sheet sport.
select 'out_of_range' as problem, query_geo, metro_code, sport
from {{ ref('search_interest') }}
where try_cast(index_value as double) < 0 or try_cast(index_value as double) > 100
union all
select 'zero_means_no_data', query_geo, metro_code, sport
from {{ ref('search_interest') }}
where try_cast(index_value as double) = 0
union all
select 'unknown_sport', query_geo, metro_code, sport
from {{ ref('search_interest') }}
where sport not in (select sport_name from {{ ref('dim_sport') }})

test.courtconnect.assert_sport_fit_sane.name: assert_sport_fit_sane
test.courtconnect.assert_sport_fit_sane.raw_code:
-- Sanity checks on the physical sport-fit reference. Returns rows only for violations.
select 'tennis should host pickleball' as failed_check
where not exists (select 1 from {{ ref('ref_sport_fit') }} where host_sport = 'Tennis' and guest_sport = 'Pickleball')
union all
select 'pickleball must not host tennis'
where exists (select 1 from {{ ref('ref_sport_fit') }} where host_sport = 'Pickleball' and guest_sport = 'Tennis')
union all
select 'a sport must not host itself'
where exists (select 1 from {{ ref('ref_sport_fit') }} where host_sport = guest_sport)

test.courtconnect.assert_sport_words_don.name: assert_sport_words_dont_double_count
test.courtconnect.assert_sport_words_don.raw_code:
-- A "Table Tennis Association" must count as Table Tennis, not also as plain Tennis (the longest matching phrase wins).
select p.place_name
from {{ ref('dim_place') }} p
join {{ ref('bridge_place_sport') }} bp on bp.place_id = p.place_id and bp.match_type = 'name_keyword'
join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_id = bp.sport_id and s.sport_name = 'Tennis'
where p.category not in ('tennis_court', 'tennis_stadium')
  and (p.place_name like '%Table Tennis%' or p.place_name like '%Platform Tennis%' or p.place_name like '%Beach Tennis%')

test.courtconnect.assert_venue_actions_f.name: assert_venue_actions_fresh

test.courtconnect.assert_venue_actions_v.name: assert_venue_actions_valid
test.courtconnect.assert_venue_actions_v.raw_code:
-- A venue action must point at a venue we hold, link out over https, and have sane dates.
select action_key, 'venue not found' as problem from {{ ref('stg_venue_actions') }} where venue_id is null
union all
select action_key, 'link is not https' from {{ ref('stg_venue_actions') }} where url is null or url not like 'https://%'
union all
select action_key, 'end before start' from {{ ref('stg_venue_actions') }} where start_date is not null and end_date is not null and end_date < start_date
union all
select action_key, 'action_key not unique'
from {{ ref('stg_venue_actions') }} group by action_key having count(*) > 1

test.courtconnect.assert_venue_confirmat.name: assert_venue_confirmations_valid
test.courtconnect.assert_venue_confirmat.raw_code:
-- A confirmation must point at a hand-added venue, carry a date and evidence, and use a handle (not an email or a spaced name).
select c.venue_key, 'venue not in manual_venues' as problem
from {{ ref('stg_venue_confirmations') }} c left join {{ ref('stg_manual_venues') }} m on m.venue_key = c.venue_key
where m.venue_key is null
union all
select venue_key, 'missing date or evidence' from {{ ref('stg_venue_confirmations') }} where confirmed_on is null or evidence is null
union all
select venue_key, 'confirmed_by must be a GitHub handle' from {{ ref('stg_venue_confirmations') }}
where confirmed_by like '%@%' or confirmed_by like '% %'
union all
select venue_key, 'same person, method and day twice' from {{ ref('stg_venue_confirmations') }}
group by venue_key, confirmed_by, method, confirmed_on having count(*) > 1

test.courtconnect.assert_wall_clusters_c.name: assert_wall_clusters_converged
test.courtconnect.assert_wall_clusters_c.raw_code:
-- Fails if any wall's group label was still changing on the final pass,
-- which would mean the grouping needs more passes (raise `passes` in int_wall_clusters).
select wall_key from {{ ref('int_wall_clusters') }} where changed_in_last_pass

test.courtconnect.assert_watch_events_fr.name: assert_watch_events_fresh

test.courtconnect.assert_watch_events_no.name: assert_watch_events_no_duplicates
test.courtconnect.assert_watch_events_no.raw_code:
-- Fails when two watch events overlap in dates and sit within 1 km of each other, so one event listed under two
-- names (an organizer page and a directory) cannot become two pins. Fix: merge the rows into one (keep the organizer's
-- page, note the other listing in source_note). If they really are different events, add the pair to `reviewed`.
with reviewed(a, b) as (
    values
        ('usa-pickleball-nationals-2026', 'usap-collegiate-series-san-diego-2026'),
        ('socal-open-tour-finals-2026', 'socal-ntrp-tour-finals-singles-2026'),
        ('national-40s-hardcourts-2026', 'national-father-son-hardcourts-2026'),
        ('btsm-winter-kickoff-classic-2026', 'btsm-vision-bt10-nov-20-2026'),
        ('btsm-winter-kickoff-classic-2026', 'btsm-vision-bt10-nov-22-2026')
)
select x.event_key as event_a, y.event_key as event_b, 'possible duplicate event (same place, overlapping dates)' as problem
from {{ ref('stg_watch_events') }} x
join {{ ref('stg_watch_events') }} y
  on x.event_key < y.event_key
 and x.start_date <= coalesce(y.end_date, y.start_date)
 and y.start_date <= coalesce(x.end_date, x.start_date)
 and sqrt(power((x.lat - y.lat) * 111.0, 2) + power((x.lon - y.lon) * 111.0 * cos(radians(x.lat)), 2)) < 1.0
where not exists (
    select 1 from reviewed r
    where (r.a = x.event_key and r.b = y.event_key) or (r.a = y.event_key and r.b = x.event_key)
)

test.courtconnect.assert_watch_events_va.name: assert_watch_events_valid

seed.courtconnect.all_racquet.name: all_racquet
seed.courtconnect.all_racquet.description: Master list of racket sports the platform supports, one row per sport. Synced from the Google Sheet (tab "All Raquet"; its location is kept in .env, not in the repo) by ingestion/sync_sports_sheet.py. Values are raw; cleaning happens in stg_sports.

sport.name: sport
sport.description: The racket sport. Every non-blank value must become a row in dim_sport.

seed.courtconnect.closed_places.name: closed_places
seed.courtconnect.closed_places.description: Overture places that no longer exist but are still listed as open. Excluded from the map. One row per place_id; each row needs `evidence` (what shows it closed) and `verified_on`.

seed.courtconnect.court_group_merge.name: court_group_merge
seed.courtconnect.court_group_merge.description: Two OSM court groups that are one facility (a club's courts mapped more than 100 m apart), merged into one venue by int_court_pairs. The duplicate-venue test flags such pairs once both groups carry the same name. Keyed by OSM court id (stable; not FK-tested because the CI fixture holds only a sample of courts); evidence says how it was checked.

seed.courtconnect.manual_venue_sport_blo.name: manual_venue_sport_blocks
seed.courtconnect.manual_venue_sport_blo.description: Question marks on hand-added venues: a sport derived through sport_also_played (Rapidball on a squash venue) is not passed on to that venue until a person identifies its access or courts. `venue_key` is the manual_venues key, `sport` the derived sport (exact name from the master list), `reason` says what is unknown. The venue's own listed sports are unaffected. Drop the row once the venue is identified.

seed.courtconnect.osm_court_sport_overri.name: osm_court_sport_overrides
seed.courtconnect.osm_court_sport_overri.description: A person found an OpenStreetMap sport tag wrong, so that court (court_id like way/123) is not counted for that sport. Optional `correct_sport`: the sport the court really is (found from imagery or a public page); it then counts for that sport at 'osm_tag_loose' strength (needs review).

seed.courtconnect.osm_sport_map.name: osm_sport_map
seed.courtconnect.osm_sport_map.description: Maps an OpenStreetMap `sport=` tag value to a sport on the master sheet, with a confidence. stg_osm_courts keeps only OSM records whose tag maps to a racket sport here. Built by ingestion/build_osm_sport_map.py.

seed.courtconnect.osm_wall_overrides.name: osm_wall_overrides
seed.courtconnect.osm_wall_overrides.description: Wall type of OpenStreetMap handball walls where imagery or a public page settles it (OSM has no wall-count tag; unlisted walls stay assumed one-wall). One row per OSM element; elements that stand together must share a type. `confirmation` is inferred for an imagery read.

seed.courtconnect.overture_category_map.name: overture_category_map
seed.courtconnect.overture_category_map.description: Overture place categories that mean a racket-sport court or club (for example tennis_court), mapped to a sport. ingestion/extract_overture_places.py reads it to decide which categories to pull.

seed.courtconnect.parent_merge_block.name: parent_merge_block
seed.courtconnect.parent_merge_block.description: A named park, school or club (as in OSM, matched on the lower-cased name) whose courts belong to different facilities, so int_court_pairs does NOT link its courts by the 'same parent within parent_merge_radius_m' rule (ADR 0030). Courts in it still join when closer than venue_radius_m or through seeds/court_group_merge.csv. One row per parent; evidence says why the courts are separate facilities and how that was checked.

seed.courtconnect.place_no_group.name: place_no_group
seed.courtconnect.place_no_group.description: Overture places that share a street address with another place but are a different business, so dim_place keeps each as its own pin.

seed.courtconnect.place_sport_overrides.name: place_sport_overrides
seed.courtconnect.place_sport_overrides.description: Human review of weak place-to-sport matches (see mart_places_to_review). One row per decision: place_id, sport (exact name from the master list), verdict ('confirm' or 'reject'), evidence (what the venue's own public page says; blank on rows from before 2026-10-14), verified_on (date checked).

seed.courtconnect.place_venue_link.name: place_venue_link
seed.courtconnect.place_venue_link.description: A hand-checked link from one Overture place to one OSM court group (any court id of the group) that is the same facility although no place-match radius reaches it, e.g. a club whose Overture pin is its street address and whose courts are mapped 400 m away inside the same park. int_place_venue_match applies it first (match_rule 'seed_link'), so the two stop showing as two pins (ADR 0031). Keyed by stable ids; not FK-tested because the CI fixture holds only a sample. Evidence says how the link was checked.

seed.courtconnect.player_groups.name: player_groups
seed.courtconnect.player_groups.description: Public player-group links (Meetup, WhatsApp, Partiful, Facebook) that a club or organizer publishes itself, kept as leads for a future groups shelf (ADR 0009 amendment 2026-10-21). Link-outs only: groups are never joined or read, no member data is stored. `published_at` is the club page or bio that carries the link; a link that stops loading is removed, not guessed at.

seed.courtconnect.player_platforms.name: player_platforms
seed.courtconnect.player_platforms.description: Player-matching apps and sites shown under "Find people to play with" (social phase A, ADR 0015). Link-outs only: nothing is scraped, no member data is stored. `evidence` quotes the public page read on `verified_on`; none of them is checked for a California, Nevada, Oregon, Washington or Hawaii player pool, and the app says so.

seed.courtconnect.search_interest.name: search_interest
seed.courtconnect.search_interest.description: Google Trends "interest by metro", hand-collected from the public Trends pages (docs/search_interest_plan.md): one row per query geo, metro and sport. index_value is relative sampled search interest, 100 = the top metro of that query (blank = Trends had no data, never 0). The California and Nevada queries use different scales; int_search_interest puts them on one. Not search volumes, not a count of players.

seed.courtconnect.search_metros.name: search_metros
seed.courtconnect.search_metros.description: The 14 Google Trends metros that cover California and Nevada (Google's metro codes) with one anchor city each. A venue belongs to the nearest anchor within 120 miles (mart_search_vs_coverage): our own approximation, NOT the Nielsen/Google metro boundaries (Nielsen owns those).

seed.courtconnect.social_events.name: social_events
seed.courtconnect.social_events.description: Recurring social get-togethers people can join (mixers, club nights, open play, social nights), curated by hand, one row per SERIES, not per date. A discovery list only: every row links out to the organizer; nothing is signed up for or paid here. `schedule` is the organizer's own wording; `last_listed_date` is the last session date their page lists (blank = no end shown); `age_focus` and `audience` are only what the organizer states, never guessed (ADR 0021). `verified_on` records when the page was last read.

seed.courtconnect.sport_aliases.name: sport_aliases
seed.courtconnect.sport_aliases.description: Alternate names for sports (editable). Used to search other sources when a sport has no OSM tag.

seed.courtconnect.sport_also_played.name: sport_also_played
seed.courtconnect.sport_also_played.description: A court or place that counts for sport `sport` also counts for `also_sport` (racquetball courts host 4-wall paddle). Derived rows are inferred, not separately observed; bridge_place_sport labels them match_type 'also_played'. `exclude_private_members` = yes skips members-only venues and club-style place names; `exclude_name_inferred` = yes skips places whose source sport was inferred from the place name. `only_surfaces` (e.g. grass;turf) limits the derived sport to courts with one of those surfaces; places and courts with an unknown surface are skipped. `only_access` (e.g. public) limits the derived sport to courts and hand-added venues with that access; unknown-access courts and Overture places (no access data) are skipped (Table Tennis -> Micro Pickleball). `same_table` = yes: the two sports share one piece of equipment and are equally valid there (Teqpong / Teqis on a Teqboard), so the map lists them together in the Plays line (one shared court count) instead of as an optional note.

seed.courtconnect.sport_play_anywhere.name: sport_play_anywhere
seed.courtconnect.sport_play_anywhere.description: Sports that need no fixed court (for example any beach), with the note the app shows. Read by ingestion/export_app_data.py; see ADR 0020.

seed.courtconnect.sport_search_terms.name: sport_search_terms
seed.courtconnect.sport_search_terms.description: Business-name words that suggest a place offers a sport, with a `reliability`: distinctive words ("padel") are strong evidence; ambiguous ones ("Real Tennis" in "Camino Real Tennis Center") are kept as weak evidence and never count as a venue until a person confirms them (mart_places_to_review). Built by ingestion/build_search_terms.py from the sheet and sport_aliases.

seed.courtconnect.venue_city_official.name: venue_city_official
seed.courtconnect.venue_city_official.description: City of a named pin that no dataset gives a city for (remote parks, schools, golf courses), read from the venue's own page or a public listing (int_venue_address, city). Keyed by venue_id with the pin's lat/lon: a row is ignored if the pin has moved. Public pages only (ADR 0007); evidence says which page and when.

seed.courtconnect.venue_confirmations.name: venue_confirmations
seed.courtconnect.venue_confirmations.description: A log of individual confirmations of venues in manual_venues, one row per person per check (ADR 0008). `confirmed_by` is a GitHub handle, never a real name or contact detail. The map shows how many different people confirmed a venue. A reviewer decides when the count justifies raising the venue's `confirmation` level in manual_venues; this file never changes it by itself. `reported` rows are word-of-mouth reports (docs/community_reports_plan.md); the map does not count them as confirmations.

seed.courtconnect.venue_court_counts.name: venue_court_counts
seed.courtconnect.venue_court_counts.description: A person's court count for one sport at one venue where the OpenStreetMap count is wrong (core.bridge_venue_sport replaces the count for a sport the venue already has, and sports derived from it follow). Keyed by venue_id with the pin's lat/lon: a row is ignored if the venue's courts are no longer there. Reported counts (imagery, owner visits) say so in evidence; public data only (ADR 0005, 0007).

seed.courtconnect.venue_name_official.name: venue_name_official
seed.courtconnect.venue_name_official.description: A name for an OSM court group that no dataset names, taken from a nearby high-confidence Overture club place (100-225 m away, so the nearest-court rule left it unlinked), checked by hand against the pin's position (core.dim_venue, name_source 'manual'). The name is INFERRED from position unless `evidence` says the club's own page was read. Keyed by venue_id with the pin's lat/lon: a row is ignored if the pin has moved. Public data only (ADR 0005, 0007).

seed.courtconnect.watch_events.name: watch_events
seed.courtconnect.watch_events.description: Pro and amateur events people can go and watch, curated by hand, one row per event. A discovery list only: every row links out to the organizer; nothing is sold or booked here. `verified_on` records when the facts were last checked.

seed.courtconnect.website_overrides.name: website_overrides
seed.courtconnect.website_overrides.description: Websites a person found to be parked, hijacked or the wrong business; DNS cannot see these. They win over the automatic check.

model.elementary.alerts_anomaly_detectio.name: alerts_anomaly_detection
model.elementary.alerts_anomaly_detectio.description: A view that is used by the Elementary CLI to generate alerts on data anomalies detected using the elementary anomaly detection tests. The view filters alerts according to configuration.
model.elementary.alerts_anomaly_detectio.raw_code:
{{ config(materialized="view", bind=False) }}

with
    elementary_test_results as (select * from {{ ref("elementary_test_results") }}),

    alerts_anomaly_detection as (
        select
            id as alert_id,
            data_issue_id,
            test_execution_id,
            test_unique_id,
            model_unique_id,
            detected_at,
            database_name,
            schema_name,
            table_name,
            column_name,
            test_type as alert_type,
            test_sub_type as sub_type,
            test_results_description as alert_description,
            owners,
            tags,
            test_results_query as alert_results_query,
            other,
            test_name,
            test_short_name,
            test_params,
            severity,
            status,
            result_rows
        from elementary_test_results
        where
            {{ elementary.render_bool_config_var("disable_test_alerts", negate=true) }}
            and lower(status) != 'pass'
            {%- if elementary.get_config_var("disable_warn_alerts") -%}
                and lower(status) != 'warn'
            {%- endif -%}
            {%- if elementary.get_config_var("disable_skipped_test_alerts") -%}
                and lower(status) != 'skipped'
            {%- endif -%}
            and test_type = 'anomaly_detection'
    )

select *
from alerts_anomaly_detection

model.elementary.alerts_dbt_models.name: alerts_dbt_models
model.elementary.alerts_dbt_models.description: A view that is used by the Elementary CLI to generate models alerts, including all the fields the alert will include such as owner, tags, error message, etc. It joins data about models and snapshots run results, and filters alerts according to configuration.
model.elementary.alerts_dbt_models.raw_code:
{{ config(materialized="view", bind=False) }}

with
    error_models as (

        select
            model_execution_id,
            unique_id,
            invocation_id,
            name,
            generated_at,
            status,
            full_refresh,
            message,
            execution_time,
            execute_started_at,
            execute_completed_at,
            compile_started_at,
            compile_completed_at,
            compiled_code,
            database_name,
            schema_name,
            materialization,
            tags,
            package_name,
            path,
            original_path,
            owner,
            alias
        from {{ ref("model_run_results") }}

        union all

        select
            model_execution_id,
            unique_id,
            invocation_id,
            name,
            generated_at,
            status,
            full_refresh,
            message,
            execution_time,
            execute_started_at,
            execute_completed_at,
            compile_started_at,
            compile_completed_at,
            compiled_code,
            database_name,
            schema_name,
            materialization,
            tags,
            package_name,
            path,
            original_path,
            owner,
            alias
        from {{ ref("snapshot_run_results") }}
    )

select
    model_execution_id as alert_id,
    unique_id,
    {{ elementary.edr_cast_as_timestamp("generated_at") }} as detected_at,
    database_name,
    materialization,
    path,
    original_path,
    schema_name,
    message,
    owner as owners,
    tags,
    alias,
    status,
    full_refresh
from error_models
where
    {{ elementary.render_bool_config_var("disable_model_alerts", negate=true) }}
    and lower(status) != 'success'
    {%- if elementary.get_config_var("disable_skipped_model_alerts") -%}
        and lower(status) != 'skipped'
    {%- endif -%}

model.elementary.alerts_dbt_source_fresh.name: alerts_dbt_source_freshness
model.elementary.alerts_dbt_source_fresh.raw_code:
{{ config(materialized="view", bind=False) }}

with
    results as (select * from {{ ref("dbt_source_freshness_results") }}),

    sources as (select * from {{ ref("dbt_sources") }})

select
    results.source_freshness_execution_id as alert_id,
    results.max_loaded_at,
    results.snapshotted_at,
    {{ elementary.edr_cast_as_timestamp("results.generated_at") }} as detected_at,
    results.max_loaded_at_time_ago_in_s,
    results.status,
    results.error,
    results.warn_after,
    results.error_after,
    results.{{ elementary.escape_reserved_keywords("filter") }},
    sources.unique_id,
    sources.database_name,
    sources.schema_name,
    sources.source_name,
    sources.identifier,
    sources.tags,
    sources.meta,
    sources.owner,
    sources.package_name,
    sources.path,
    -- These columns below are deprecated. We add them since this view
    -- was used to be loaded into an incremental model with those columns, their names
    -- were later changed
    -- and Databricks doesn't respect `on_schema_change = 'append_new_columns'`
    -- properly, as described here -
    -- https://docs.databricks.com/en/delta/update-schema.html#automatic-schema-evolution-for-delta-lake-merge
    results.error_after as freshness_error_after,
    results.warn_after as freshness_warn_after,
    results.{{ elementary.escape_reserved_keywords("filter") }} as freshness_filter
from results
join sources on results.unique_id = sources.unique_id
where
    {{
        elementary.render_bool_config_var(
            "disable_source_freshness_alerts", negate=true
        )
    }} and lower(status) != 'pass'

model.elementary.alerts_dbt_tests.name: alerts_dbt_tests
model.elementary.alerts_dbt_tests.description: A view that is used by the Elementary CLI to generate dbt tests alerts, including all the fields the alert will include such as owner, tags, error message, etc. This view includes data about all dbt tests except elementary tests. It filters alerts according to configuration.
model.elementary.alerts_dbt_tests.raw_code:
{{ config(materialized="view", bind=False) }}

with
    elementary_test_results as (select * from {{ ref("elementary_test_results") }}),

    alerts_dbt_tests as (
        select
            id as alert_id,
            data_issue_id,
            test_execution_id,
            test_unique_id,
            model_unique_id,
            detected_at,
            database_name,
            schema_name,
            table_name,
            column_name,
            test_type as alert_type,
            test_sub_type as sub_type,
            test_results_description as alert_description,
            owners,
            tags,
            test_results_query as alert_results_query,
            other,
            test_name,
            test_short_name,
            test_params,
            severity,
            status,
            result_rows
        from elementary_test_results
        where
            {{ elementary.render_bool_config_var("disable_test_alerts", negate=true) }}
            and lower(status) != 'pass'
            {% if elementary.get_config_var("disable_warn_alerts") %}
                and lower(status) != 'warn'
            {% endif %}
            {% if elementary.get_config_var("disable_skipped_test_alerts") %}
                and lower(status) != 'skipped'
            {% endif %}
            and test_type = 'dbt_test'

model.elementary.alerts_schema_changes.description: A view that is used by the Elementary CLI to generate alerts on schema changes detected using elementary tests. The view filters alerts according to configuration.
model.elementary.alerts_schema_changes.raw_code:
{{
    config(
        materialized="view",
        bind=False,
    )
}}


with
    elementary_test_results as (select * from {{ ref("elementary_test_results") }}),

    alerts_schema_changes as (
        select
            id as alert_id,
            data_issue_id,
            test_execution_id,
            test_unique_id,
            model_unique_id,
            detected_at,
            database_name,
            schema_name,
            table_name,
            column_name,
            test_type as alert_type,
            test_sub_type as sub_type,
            test_results_description as alert_description,
            owners,
            tags,
            test_results_query as alert_results_query,
            other,
            test_name,
            test_short_name,
            test_params,
            severity,
            status,
            result_rows
        from elementary_test_results
        where
            {{ elementary.render_bool_config_var("disable_test_alerts", negate=true) }}
            and lower(status) != 'pass'
            {%- if elementary.get_config_var("disable_warn_alerts") -%}
                and lower(status) != 'warn'
            {%- endif -%}
            {%- if elementary.get_config_var("disable_skipped_test_alerts") -%}
                and lower(status) != 'skipped'
            {%- endif -%}
            and test_type = 'schema_change'
    )

This can help you decide if there is a need to adjust the `anomaly_score_threshold`.

model.elementary.metrics_anomaly_score.name: metrics_anomaly_score
model.elementary.metrics_anomaly_score.description: This is a view on `data_monitoring_metrics` that runs the same query the anomaly detection tests run to calculate anomaly scores. The purpose of this view is to provide visibility to the results of anomaly detection tests.
model.elementary.metrics_anomaly_score.raw_code:
{{ config(materialized="view", bind=False) }}

with
    data_monitoring_metrics as (select * from {{ ref("data_monitoring_metrics") }}),

    time_window_aggregation as (

        select
            id,
            full_table_name,
            column_name,
            dimension,
            dimension_value,
            metric_name,
            metric_value,
            source_value,
            bucket_start,
            bucket_end,
            bucket_duration_hours,
            updated_at,
            avg(metric_value) over (
                partition by
                    metric_name,
                    full_table_name,
                    column_name,
                    dimension,
                    dimension_value
                order by bucket_start asc
                rows between unbounded preceding and current row
            ) as training_avg,
            {{ elementary.standard_deviation("metric_value") }} over (
                partition by
                    metric_name,
                    full_table_name,
                    column_name,
                    dimension,
                    dimension_value
                order by bucket_start asc
                rows between unbounded preceding and current row
            ) as training_stddev,
            count(metric_value) over (
                partition by
                    metric_name,
                    full_table_name,
                    column_name,
                    dimension,
                    dimension_value
                order by bucket_start asc
                rows between unbounded preceding and current row
            ) as training_set_size,
            last_value(bucket_end) over (
                partition by
                    metric_name,
                    full_table_name,
                    column_name,
                    dimension,
                    dimension_value
                order by bucket_start asc
                rows between unbounded preceding and current row
            ) training_end,
            first_value(bucket_end) over (
                partition by
                    metric_name,
                    full_table_name,
                    column_name,
                    dimension,
                    dimension_value
                order by bucket_start asc
                rows between unbounded preceding and current row
            ) as training_start
        from data_monitoring_metrics
        group by
            id,
            full_table_name,
            column_name,
            dimension,
            dimension_value,
            metric_name,
            metric_value,
            source_value,
            bucket_start,
            bucket_end,
            bucket_duration_hours,
            updated_at
    ),

    time_window_scored as (

        select
            *,
            case
                when {{ elementary.edr_normalize_stddev("training_stddev") }} is null
                then null
                when training_set_size = 1
                then null  -- Single value case - no historical context for anomaly detection
                when {{ elementary.edr_normalize_stddev("training_stddev") }} = 0
                then 0  -- Stationary data case - valid, all values are identical
                else
                    (metric_value - training_avg)
                    / ({{ elementary.edr_normalize_stddev("training_stddev") }})
            end as anomaly_score
        from time_window_aggregation

    ),

    metrics_anomaly_score as (

        select
            id,
            full_table_name,
            column_name,
            dimension,
            dimension_value,
            metric_name,
            anomaly_score,
            metric_value as latest_metric_value,
            bucket_start,
            bucket_end,
            training_avg,
            training_stddev,
            training_start,
            training_end,
            training_set_size,
            max(updated_at) as updated_at
        from time_window_scored
        where
            metric_value is not null
            and training_avg is not null
            and bucket_end
            >= {{
                elementary.edr_timeadd(
                    "day",
                    "-7",
                    elementary.edr_date_trunc(
                        "day", elementary.edr_current_timestamp()
                    ),
                )
            }}
        group by
            id,
            full_table_name,
            column_name,
            dimension,
            dimension_value,
            metric_name,
            anomaly_score,
            metric_value,
            bucket_start,
            bucket_end,
            training_avg,
            training_stddev,
            training_start,
            training_end,
            training_set_size

    ),

    final as (

        select
            id,
            full_table_name,
            column_name,
            dimension,
            dimension_value,
            metric_name,
            anomaly_score,
            latest_metric_value,
            bucket_start,
            bucket_end,
            training_avg,
            training_stddev,
            training_start,
            training_end,
            training_set_size,
            updated_at,
            {{
                elementary.edr_condition_as_boolean(
                    "abs(anomaly_score) > "
                    ~ elementary.get_config_var("anomaly_sensitivity")
                )
            }} as is_anomaly
        from metrics_anomaly_score
    )

select *
from final

{{ config(materialized="view", bind=False) }}

{%- set day_partition = elementary.edr_time_trunc("day", "run_results.generated_at") -%}
{%- set day_window = (
    "over (partition by "
    ~ day_partition
    ~ " order by run_results.generated_at asc rows between unbounded preceding and unbounded following)"
) -%}
{%- set first_inv_cond = (
    "first_value(invocation_id) " ~ day_window ~ " = invocation_id"
) -%}
{%- set last_inv_cond = (
    "last_value(invocation_id) " ~ day_window ~ " = invocation_id"
) -%}

with
    dbt_run_results as (select * from {{ ref("dbt_run_results") }}),

    dbt_models as (select * from {{ ref("dbt_models") }})

select
    run_results.model_execution_id,
    run_results.unique_id,
    run_results.invocation_id,
    run_results.query_id,
    run_results.name,
    run_results.generated_at,
    run_results.created_at,
    run_results.status,
    run_results.full_refresh,
    run_results.message,
    run_results.execution_time,
    run_results.execute_started_at,
    run_results.execute_completed_at,
    run_results.compile_started_at,
    run_results.compile_completed_at,
    run_results.compiled_code,
    run_results.adapter_response,
    run_results.thread_id,
    run_results.group_name,
    models.database_name,
    models.schema_name,
    coalesce(run_results.materialization, models.materialization) as materialization,
    models.tags,
    models.package_name,
    models.path,
    models.original_path,
    models.owner,
    models.alias,
    row_number() over (
        partition by run_results.unique_id order by run_results.generated_at desc
    ) as model_invocation_reverse_index,
    {{ elementary.edr_condition_as_boolean(first_inv_cond) }}
    as is_the_first_invocation_of_the_day,
    {{ elementary.edr_condition_as_boolean(last_inv_cond) }}
    as is_the_last_invocation_of_the_day

from dbt_run_results run_results
join dbt_models models on run_results.unique_id = models.unique_id

model.courtconnect.int_venue_sport_court.name: int_venue_sport_courts
model.courtconnect.int_venue_sport_court.description: Which sports are played at which court venue and which court source says so (the former bridge_venue_sport body). core.bridge_venue_sport adds the hitting-wall rows (ADR 0032).
model.courtconnect.int_venue_sport_court.raw_code:
-- Which sports are played at COURT venues, and which source says so (core.bridge_venue_sport adds the hitting-wall rows, ADR 0032).
-- OSM contributes court counts; places contribute only STRONG evidence (a racket category or a distinctive sport word);
-- manual venues are hand-curated entries. Weak name matches stay in bridge_place_sport and mart_places_to_review.
with osm as (
    select
        c.venue_id,
        b.sport_id,
        count(distinct case when c.record_kind = 'court' then c.court_id end) as courts
    from {{ ref('dim_court') }} c
    join {{ ref('bridge_court_sport') }} b on b.court_id = c.court_id
    group by 1, 2
),

places as (
    select distinct p.venue_id, bp.sport_id
    from {{ ref('dim_place') }} p
    join {{ ref('bridge_place_sport') }} bp on bp.place_id = p.place_id and bp.evidence = 'strong'
),

-- A manual venue attaches to the venue it matched (see int_manual_venue_match). Its court count is per sport (a park's OSM
-- courts may be tennis while the hand-added ones are paddle tennis), and where both sources count the same sport we take the
-- larger number instead of adding them.
manual as (
    select
        mm.effective_venue_id                                 as venue_id,
        s.sport_id,
        coalesce(max(m.courts_count), 0)                      as courts,
        string_agg(distinct m.surface_type, ';')              as surfaces,
        string_agg(distinct m.access_type, ';')               as access_types
    from {{ ref('stg_manual_venues') }} m
    join {{ ref('int_manual_venue_match') }} mm on mm.venue_key = m.venue_key
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_name = m.sport_name
    group by mm.effective_venue_id, s.sport_id
),

-- Sports a hand-curated venue lists also pass on their also-played sports (a pickleball seed row makes the venue a Skyball venue, like
-- an OSM pickleball court does). These rows are derived, so they carry no source flag; the finder mart drops the exclude_private_members
-- ones at members-only venues.
manual_also as (
    select m.venue_id, d.sport_id, m.courts
    from manual m
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} f on f.sport_id = m.sport_id
    join {{ ref('sport_also_played') }} a on trim(a.sport) = f.sport_name
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} d on d.sport_name = trim(a.also_sport)
    -- only_surfaces set (Soft Tennis: grass;turf): the hand-added venue must list one of those surfaces
    where (nullif(trim(a.only_surfaces), '') is null
           or list_has_any(string_split(m.surfaces, ';'), string_split(replace(a.only_surfaces, ' ', ''), ';')))
      -- only_access set (Micro Pickleball: public): the hand-added venue must be marked with one of those access values
      and (nullif(trim(a.only_access), '') is null
           or list_has_any(string_split(m.access_types, ';'), string_split(replace(a.only_access, ' ', ''), ';')))
      -- manual_venue_sport_blocks.csv: a person marked this venue's derived sport as a question mark (access or court unidentified)
      and not exists (
          select 1
          from {{ ref('manual_venue_sport_blocks') }} k
          join {{ ref('int_manual_venue_match') }} km on km.venue_key = trim(k.venue_key)
          where km.effective_venue_id = m.venue_id and trim(k.sport) = d.sport_name
      )
),

unioned as (
    select venue_id, sport_id, courts, 1 as in_osm, 0 as in_places, 0 as in_manual from osm
    union all
    select venue_id, sport_id, 0, 0, 1, 0 from places
    union all
    select venue_id, sport_id, courts, 0, 0, 1 from manual
    union all
    select venue_id, sport_id, courts, 0, 0, 0 from manual_also
),

base as (
    select
        venue_id,
        sport_id,
        max(courts)                                           as courts,
        max(in_osm) = 1                                       as in_osm,
        max(in_places) = 1                                    as in_places,
        max(in_manual) = 1                                    as in_manual
    from unioned
    group by 1, 2
),

-- A person counted the courts of one sport at a venue and the OSM count is wrong (seeds/venue_court_counts.csv, e.g. 3 tennis-shaped pads
-- where imagery shows 2 tennis courts and the rest pickleball). Replaces the count only for a sport the venue already has, and only while
-- the pin is where it was checked (a row is ignored if no court of the venue lies within ~70 m of the checked position).
counted as (
    select o.venue_id, s.sport_id, cast(o.courts as integer) as courts
    from {{ ref('venue_court_counts') }} o
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} s on s.sport_name = trim(o.sport)
    where exists (
        select 1 from {{ ref('dim_court') }} c
        where c.venue_id = o.venue_id
          and abs(c.lat - cast(o.lat as double)) < 0.0007 and abs(c.lon - cast(o.lon as double)) < 0.0007)
),

-- Sports derived from the counted one (tennis courts also count for Frescotennis, Loboton, ...) follow it, but only where their count was just
-- the counted sport's own (a Skyball count raised by real pickleball courts is left alone).
cascaded as (
    select b.venue_id, b.sport_id, c.courts
    from counted c
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} f on f.sport_id = c.sport_id
    join {{ ref('sport_also_played') }} a on trim(a.sport) = f.sport_name
    join {{ ref('dim_sport') }} d on d.sport_name = trim(a.also_sport)
    join base src on src.venue_id = c.venue_id and src.sport_id = c.sport_id
    join base b on b.venue_id = c.venue_id and b.sport_id = d.sport_id and b.courts = src.courts
),

replacements as (
    select venue_id, sport_id, courts from counted
    union
    select venue_id, sport_id, courts from cascaded
)

select
    b.venue_id,
    b.sport_id,
    coalesce(r.courts, b.courts)                              as courts,
    b.in_osm,
    b.in_places,
    b.in_manual,
    false                                                     as in_wall
from base b
left join replacements r on r.venue_id = b.venue_id and r.sport_id = b.sport_id

model.courtconnect.int_venue_court.name: int_venue_court
model.courtconnect.int_venue_court.description: One row per court facility (the former dim_venue body): OSM courts grouped by proximity, Overture places and hand-added rows, venue_kind 'courts'. core.dim_venue unions it with int_wall_venue (ADR 0032). Split out so hitting walls can link to court venues without a dependency cycle.
model.courtconnect.int_venue_court.raw_code:
-- One row per court facility (ADR 0032: core.dim_venue unions this with the hitting-wall venues from int_wall_venue).
--   venue_source 'osm'         : courts grouped by proximity (ADR 0003), no matching place
--   venue_source 'osm+places'  : the same, plus an Overture place within `place_match_radius_m` that adds a name, website, phone, address
--   venue_source 'places_only' : a racket-sport place Overture knows about that OpenStreetMap has no court for (indoor clubs, gyms...)
-- Name precedence: tagged on the court > operator > Overture place name (confidence >= 0.5) > enclosing park/school/club
-- (approximate, ADR 0004) > unnamed.
with courts as (
    select * from {{ ref('dim_court') }}
),

sports as (
    select venue_id, count(distinct sport_id) as sport_count
    from {{ ref('int_venue_sport_courts') }}
    group by 1
),

best_parent as (
    select venue_id, parent_name, parent_kind
    from (
        select venue_id, parent_name, parent_kind,
               row_number() over (partition by venue_id order by parent_area asc, parent_name) as rn
        from courts
        where parent_name is not null
    ) x
    where rn = 1
),

best_place as (
    select matched_venue_id as venue_id, place_name, website, phone, address_line, city, confidence
    from (
        select *, row_number() over (partition by matched_venue_id order by confidence desc, place_id) as rn
        from {{ ref('dim_place') }}
        where matched_venue_id is not null and has_strong_sport
    ) x
    where rn = 1
),

-- Hand-added venues that matched a venue we already hold (int_manual_venue_match): they enrich it, they do not duplicate it.
best_manual as (
    select
        mm.effective_venue_id                                 as venue_id,
        min(m.venue_name)                                     as venue_name,
        min(m.website)                                        as website,
        min(m.offerings)                                      as offerings,
        max(case when m.access_type = 'public' then 1 else 0 end) = 1 as is_public,
        max(case when m.access_type in ('private', 'members') then 1 else 0 end) = 1 as is_members
    from {{ ref('stg_manual_venues') }} m
    join {{ ref('int_manual_venue_match') }} mm on mm.venue_key = m.venue_key
    where mm.is_matched
    group by mm.effective_venue_id
),

osm_venues as (
    select
        venue_id,
        -- digit-only court names ("1", "2") are court numbers, not venue names
        min(case when translate(court_name, '0123456789 ', '') <> '' then court_name end) as tagged_name,
        min(operator_name)                                    as operator_name,
        sum(case when record_kind = 'court' then 1 else 0 end)    as court_records,
        sum(case when record_kind = 'facility' then 1 else 0 end) as facility_records,
        avg(lat)                                              as lat,
        avg(lon)                                              as lon,
        min(website)                                          as website,
        min(phone)                                            as phone,
        min(opening_hours)                                    as opening_hours,
        min(address_line)                                     as address_line,
        min(city)                                             as city,
        min(region)                                           as region,   -- one venue, one region (a cluster on the border takes the first code)
        max(case when is_lit then 1 else 0 end) = 1                   as has_lit_courts,
        max(case when access_type = 'public' then 1 else 0 end) = 1   as is_confirmed_public,
        max(case when access_type in ('private', 'members') then 1 else 0 end) = 1 as has_members_courts,
        max(case when is_free then 1 else 0 end) = 1                  as has_free_courts,
        -- indoor is three-valued: true (a court is tagged indoor), false (a court is tagged outdoor/covered, none indoor), null = unknown
        -- (untagged pitches are 'likely_outdoor', an assumption, so they do not count as evidence)
        case when max(case when setting = 'indoor' then 1 else 0 end) = 1 then true
             when max(case when setting in ('outdoor', 'covered') then 1 else 0 end) = 1 then false end as has_indoor,
        max(case when setting in ('outdoor', 'likely_outdoor', 'covered') then 1 else 0 end) = 1 as has_outdoor,
        max(case when surface_type = 'hard' then 1 else 0 end) = 1    as has_hard,
        max(case when surface_type = 'clay' then 1 else 0 end) = 1    as has_clay,
        max(case when surface_type = 'grass' then 1 else 0 end) = 1   as has_grass,
        max(case when surface_type = 'turf' then 1 else 0 end) = 1    as has_turf,
        max(case when surface_type = 'sand' then 1 else 0 end) = 1    as has_sand,
        max(case when surface_type in ('carpet', 'wood') then 1 else 0 end) = 1 as has_indoor_floor
    from courts
    group by venue_id
),

-- A hand-checked name for a court group a nearby club place names (seeds/venue_name_official.csv); counts only while the pin is where it was checked.
-- places_only pins use the same seed below (a club listing that sits on a public building, e.g. Balboa Park Activity Center).
official_name as (
    select o.venue_id, o.venue_name
    from {{ ref('venue_name_official') }} o
    join osm_venues v on v.venue_id = o.venue_id
    where abs(v.lat - cast(o.lat as double)) < 0.0003 and abs(v.lon - cast(o.lon as double)) < 0.0003
),

osm_final as (
    select
        v.venue_id,
        coalesce(v.tagged_name, v.operator_name, bm.venue_name, on_.venue_name,
                 case when pl.confidence >= 0.5 then pl.place_name end, pp.parent_name)   as venue_name,
        case
            when v.tagged_name is not null                      then 'court_name'
            when v.operator_name is not null                    then 'operator'
            when bm.venue_name is not null                      then 'manual'
            when on_.venue_name is not null                     then 'manual'
            when pl.confidence >= 0.5                           then 'places_directory'
            when pp.parent_name is not null                     then 'enclosing_feature'
            else 'unnamed'
        end                                                   as name_source,
        case when v.tagged_name is null and v.operator_name is null and bm.venue_name is null and on_.venue_name is null
                  and coalesce(pl.confidence, 0) < 0.5 then pp.parent_kind end            as name_feature_kind,
        case when pl.venue_id is not null then 'osm+places' else 'osm' end                as venue_source,
        v.court_records,
        v.facility_records,
        v.lat, v.lon,
        coalesce(v.website, bm.website, pl.website)           as website,
        coalesce(v.phone, pl.phone)                           as phone,
        v.opening_hours,
        coalesce(v.address_line, pl.address_line)             as address_line,
        coalesce(v.city, pl.city)                             as city,
        v.region,
        bm.offerings                                          as offerings,
        v.has_lit_courts, (v.is_confirmed_public or coalesce(bm.is_public, false)) as is_confirmed_public, v.has_free_courts,
        -- members-only = marked private/members and nothing says public (the only access signal we hold; unmarked venues are NOT assumed public)
        ((v.has_members_courts or coalesce(bm.is_members, false)) and not (v.is_confirmed_public or coalesce(bm.is_public, false))) as is_members_only,
        v.has_indoor, v.has_outdoor,
        case when v.has_indoor is not null then 'osm_tag' else 'unknown' end              as indoor_basis,
        v.has_hard, v.has_clay, v.has_grass, v.has_turf, v.has_sand, v.has_indoor_floor,
        cast(null as varchar)                                 as also_listed_as
    from osm_venues v
    left join best_parent pp on pp.venue_id = v.venue_id
    left join best_place pl on pl.venue_id = v.venue_id
    left join best_manual bm on bm.venue_id = v.venue_id
    left join official_name on_ on on_.venue_id = v.venue_id
),

-- Places that share an address are one venue (dim_place.venue_id): the best-confidence record names it, the others are
-- kept as `also_listed_as`, and a website/phone missing on the best record is taken from the others.
places_ranked as (
    select
        p.*,
        row_number() over (
            partition by p.venue_id
            order by p.confidence desc, case when p.website is not null then 0 else 1 end, p.place_id
        ) as rn
    from {{ ref('dim_place') }} p
    where p.matched_venue_id is null and p.has_strong_sport
),

place_group_extra as (
    select
        venue_id,
        min(website)                                                          as any_website,
        min(phone)                                                            as any_phone,
        min(address_line)                                                     as any_address,
